g12-biology.t: Suppose a couple produced a legitimate child of blood type B, what are the genotypes of the couple?
g12-biology.e: A child of blood type B must inherit at least one I B allele. Among the choices, only the cross AO × BO can yield offspring with the BO genotype, which expresses as blood type B.

g12-biology.t: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are important, EXCEPT
o: adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.
tilting the lid of the Petri dish during inoculation.
g12-biology.e: Adding distilled water to a sterilized agar medium after autoclaving would introduce external microbial contaminants, compromising the sterile culture environment.

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following is true about the substance represented by the chemical formula C2 H5 NO2 ?
​
g12-biology.e: The formula C2H5NO2 corresponds to glycine, the simplest amino acid, which contains an amino group (-NH2) and a carboxyl group (-COOH).

g12-biology.t:
Secretions of endocrine glands require receptors on cell membrane to be picked by their targets while exocrine
secretions do not. This is because
o: exocrine glands secrete hormone directly to the blood stream.
endocrine glands are controlled by the nervous system.
g12-biology.e: Because endocrine glands are ductless, they secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream to circulate throughout the body; target cells must express specific receptors to detect and respond to these systemic signals.

g12-biology.t: What happens if the axon is stimulated? Formation of
o: positive charge outside of the axon
negative charge in both sides of the axon
g12-biology.e: When an axon is stimulated, sodium channels open and sodium ions (N a+ ) rush inward, causing depolarization and the generation of a positive charge inside the axon.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is the common idea held by all the creationists?
o: All life was created in six days.
Life came to earth from elsewhere in the universe.
Life was created by a supernatural being.
g12-biology.e: While creationists may differ on the timeline and mechanism of creation, the defining belief common to all creationism is that life was created by a supernatural being.

g12-biology.t:
Suppose the fibers in the connective tissue of the skin and blood vessels do not form properly and causes
bleeding gums and poor healing of wounds. This problem is related with deficiency of
g12-biology.e: Vitamin C is essential for synthesizing collagen. Deficiency leads to scurvy, causing bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

g12-biology.t:
70. Which part of plant leaf contain large number of chloroplasts that carry out most of the photosynthetic
activity?
g12-biology.e: The palisade mesophyll consists of column-shaped cells packed with a high concentration of chloroplasts, making it the primary site of light absorption and photosynthesis in a leaf.

g12-biology.t: Which technological products have been made through imitation of termite mound architecture?
g12-biology.e: A termite mound stays close to one temperature all day, because its chimneys and side tunnels let warm air rise out and cool air enter low down. Architects copied that flow of air in buildings such as the Eastgate Centre in Harare, which stays cool with very little air conditioning. New drone design is the tempting answer, but drones copy the flight of birds and insects, not a mound.

g12-biology.t:
Grade 9 students identified an organism using dichotomous keys. The organism was poikilothermic, invertebrate
and had six jointed legs. To which phylum would the students group this organism?
g12-biology.e: Organisms with a segmented body, jointed appendages (six legs), and an exoskeleton belong to the phylum Arthropoda.

g12-biology.t: What is the term that describes plant response towards touch or physical contact?
g12-biology.e: Thigmotropism is the directional growth response of a plant in reaction to touch or physical contact with a solid object, such as climbing vines wrapping around a support.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following nucleotide sequences contains four pyrimidine bases?
g12-biology.e: Pyrimidines are cytosine (C), thymine (T), and uracil (U). In GATCAATGC, the pyrimidines are T, C, T, and C, totaling exactly four.

g12-biology.t: Why does photorespiration take place in a hot environment? Because plants close their stomata and face
g12-biology.e: Under hot and dry conditions, plants close their stomata to prevent water loss, which blocks carbon dioxide from entering the leaf, leading to a CO2 shortage that triggers photorespiration.

g12-biology.t: All of the following are examples of innate behaviours EXCEPT
o: training killer whales at marine parks.
producing tears when dust gets into the eyes.
a fly moving its maggot into more humid environment.
g12-biology.e: Training killer whales at marine parks involves operant conditioning, which is a form of learned behavior rather than an innate behavior.

g12-biology.t: Herpes simplex is a type of
g12-biology.e: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) is a double-stranded DNA virus belonging to the Herpesviridae family, meaning its genetic material is DNA rather than RNA.

g12-biology.t:
Among the following ABO blood group genotype, which one produces two types which one produces two types
of antigens?
g12-biology.e: The genotype IA IB exhibits codominance, meaning both alleles are fully expressed to produce both A and B surface antigens on red blood cells.

g12-biology.t:
If someone suddenly removes his/her hand from a very hot object, which of the following types of behavior is
manifested?
g12-biology.e: The rapid and automatic withdrawal of a hand from a painful hot stimulus is an innate spinal reflex action that protects the body from tissue damage.

g12-biology.t:
In Ethiopia, which of the following genera of microorganisms has the potential to be used for single cell protein
production?
g12-biology.e: Spirulina is a genus of blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) that grows abundantly in Ethiopian alkaline lakes (like Lake Chitu) and is widely cultivated as a rich source of single-cell protein (SCP)

g12-biology.t: Which of the following processes explains lactate production during anaerobic respiration in animal cells?
g12-biology.e: Lactate is produced during anaerobic respiration in animal cells by the reduction of pyruvate using electrons from NADH, a reaction catalyzed by lactate dehydrogenase.

g12-biology.t: What does an ethnologist study?
g12-biology.e: Although misspelled as 'ethnologist', the question refers to an ethologist, a scientist who studies animal behavior in natural environments.

g12-biology.t: What is the shape of an enzyme molecule?
g12-biology.e: Enzymes are tertiary or quaternary proteins that fold into a compact, three-dimensional globular shape.

g12-biology.t:
Which drop of iodine solution is added to a solution of a foodstuff and the foodstuff turns dark blue what dose
the foodstuff contain
g12-biology.e: Iodine solution reacts specifically with starch to form a characteristic dark blue or blue-black complex.

g12-biology.t:
If the protoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall when a plant cell is bathed in a sugar solution, what is the
concentration of the solution relative to the protoplasm of the plant cell?
g12-biology.e: Plasmolysis, where the protoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall, occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution because water leaves the cell by osmosis down its concentration gradient. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which of the following happens during the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
g12-biology.e: During the light-independent (dark) reactions or the Calvin cycle, carbon dioxide is fixed into organic molecules using ATP and NADPH produced during the light reactions.

g12-biology.t:
If a country has a large number of young people relative to the number of old people, to which category of
countries does it belong?
g12-biology.e: Developing countries typically have a broad-based population pyramid characterized by a high proportion of young dependents and a low proportion of elderly people due to high birth rates. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Based on similarity in number of amino acids found in haemoglobin, which one of the following animals has
closer phylogenetic relations to human beings?
g12-biology.e: Gibbons are primates (apes) and share the closest evolutionary relationship to humans among the options, having only a few amino acid differences in their haemoglobin chains compared to humans.

g12-biology.t:
Current human concerns such as famine, pestilence, and environmental degradation would be solved through
the use of:
g12-biology.e: According to the Ethiopian Grade 11 Biology curriculum, pressing global issues such as famine, pestilence, and environmental degradation can be addressed through the comprehensive application of biological principles.

g12-biology.t:
A biome characterized by its frozen soil, cold temperature, dry precipitation and inhabited by lichens and
migrating animals?
g12-biology.e: The tundra biome is characterized by permafrost (permanently frozen soil), extremely cold and dry conditions, and vegetation dominated by lichens and mosses, with highly migratory animal populations.

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following bases are the triplets of codes in the mRNA That cease translation and the ribosome
folds the polypeptide into its Final structure?
g12-biology.e: UAA, UAG and UGA are the three stop codons. They code for no amino acid, so when the ribosome reaches one of them translation ends and the finished polypeptide is released to fold. Any triplet containing T cannot be an mRNA codon, because RNA uses uracil (U) in place of thymine (T). That removes options B and C, and the triplets in D all code for amino acids.

g12-biology.t: Which type of learnt behavior is developed after a repeated exposure to a stimulus?
g12-biology.e: Habituation is a simple form of learning where an animal stops or decreases its response to a stimulus after repeated exposure to it, provided the stimulus is neither beneficial nor harmful.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is not an industrial use of bacteria?
g12-biology.e: The recycling of minerals through ecosystems is a natural biogeochemical process, not an industrial or commercial application of bacteria.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following biomes supports the highest diversity of plant and animal life?
g12-biology.e: Tropical rain forests support the highest biodiversity of any terrestrial biome due to year-round warm temperatures, ample sunlight, and high precipitation.

g12-biology.t:
A student made a collection of plants having flowers and seeds from his locality and compared their embryo,
leaves and stems using hand lens. He found that all his collections contain a single seed leaf embryo, long and
thin with parallel veins of leaves and stem contains scattered vascular bundles. Which option contains plants
that can be categorized under his collection?
g12-biology.e: One seed leaf (cotyledon), long narrow leaves with parallel veins and scattered vascular bundles in the stem are the marks of monocot plants. Grasses, orchids, teff and maize are all monocots, so option D fits the whole collection. The other options fail because roses, beans and sunflowers are dicots: they have two seed leaves, net shaped veins and vascular bundles arranged in a ring.

g12-biology.t:
If the average diameter of the human red blood cell is 0.000007 m, which one is its correct diameter when
expressed in a smaller unit?
g12-biology.e: The value 0.000007 m is equal to 7 × 10−6 m or 7μm. To convert this to nanometers, multiply by 103 , yielding 7000 nm.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following parts of the flower did Mendel remove from young flowers to prevent self-population ?
g12-biology.e: Mendel removed the immature stamens (the male reproductive organs containing pollen) from pea flowers to prevent self-pollination during his hybridization experiments.

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following enzymes is responsible to catalyze the joining of two molecules by hydrolysis of
ATP?
g12-biology.e: Ligases are enzymes that catalyze the joining (ligation) of two large molecules by forming a new chemical bond, a process usually powered by the hydrolysis of ATP. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following practices is a part of a responsible HIV/AIDS engagement in the fight against it?
o: Washing hands after shaking HIV positive individuals
Sharing needles only with close friends
g12-biology.e: Maintaining a monogamous relationship prevents the transmission of HIV, whereas sharing needles (even with friends) is highly risky, and washing hands is unnecessary as HIV is not transmitted via casual skin contact. (1)

g12-biology.t:
If an F1 round yellow pea of Rr Yy genotype is selfed, which class of pea is the most frequent in the F2
generation?
​
​
​
g12-biology.e: In a dihybrid cross of a selfed Rr Yy heterozygote, the expected phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation is 9:3:3:1, where the double dominant phenotype (Round yellow) is the most frequent at 9/16. ​ ​ ​

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following characteristic is UNNECESSARY for an object to be considered a living thing?
g12-biology.e: Locomotion (the ability to move from place to place) is not a universal characteristic of life, as plants and many fungi and sessile animals do not possess it.

g12-biology.t: which of the following is an inorganic molecule?
g12-biology.e: Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is classified as an inorganic compound; carbonates, oxides of carbon, and cyanides are standard exceptions to carbon-containing organic molecules.

g12-biology.t: Which one is the viral symmetry refers to the shape with 20 triangular faces and 12 corners?
g12-biology.e: An icosahedron is a solid with 20 triangular faces and 12 corners, and many viruses build their protein coat in that shape because identical protein units can pack into it neatly. Helical symmetry is the tempting answer, but that gives a rod or a spiral, as in the tobacco mosaic virus.

g12-biology.t: What is the important role played by microorganism such as bacteria and fungi in the ecosystem?
g12-biology.e: Bacteria and fungi are the decomposers. They break down dead bodies, fallen leaves and waste, and in doing so they release the carbon, nitrogen and minerals locked in that material back into the soil and the air where plants can take them up again. Without them the nutrients would stay trapped in dead matter and the cycle would stop. Forming organic substances is the tempting answer, but building organic matter from simple raw materials is the work of green plants and other producers. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which of the following organs serves as a coordinating system in a reflex action?
g12-biology.e: In a simple reflex arc, the spinal cord acts as the central coordinating/integrating organ that receives sensory input and directly sends motor output, bypassing the conscious brain.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following diseases increases the likelihood of contracting HIV?
g12-biology.e: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection that causes genital ulcers, which break the skin barrier and greatly facilitate the transmission and contraction of HIV.

g12-biology.t:
To which category of behavior does the human behavior that involves the strengthening of existing responses or 
the formation of new responses to existing stimuli that occur because of practice or repetition belong?
g12-biology.e: Behavior that is modified, strengthened, or acquired through practice, experience, or repetition is classified as learned behavior.

g12-biology.t: The ultimate source of genetic variation is:
g12-biology.e: Mutation is the ultimate source of all genetic variation because it introduces completely new alleles into a gene pool.

g12-biology.t: What is one of the main uses of biotechnology in food production?
g12-biology.e: Genetic engineering of crops is the main use of biotechnology in food production. Genes are added to give pest resistance, tolerance of drought or salt, longer shelf life or better nutrient content, as in vitamin A enriched rice. Option B tempts because industry does make chemicals, but making synthetic chemicals is an industrial chemical process and does not involve living systems. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following Ethiopian biological research institutes is known for housing a major gene bank in
Africa?
g12-biology.e: The Institute of Biodiversity Conservation (today called the Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute) keeps one of the largest gene banks in Africa. A gene bank stores seeds and other genetic material so that Ethiopia's crop varieties and wild species are not lost. The other choices are a university department and medical research institutes; storing genetic resources is not their job.

g12-biology.t: The sheep 'dolly' is an example of which biotechnological manipulation of animals by human?
g12-biology.e: Dolly was made by somatic cell nuclear transfer. The nucleus of a body cell taken from one adult sheep was placed into an egg cell whose own nucleus had been removed, and the embryo that grew carried the same nuclear DNA as that adult, so Dolly was a clone. Genetically engineered animal is the tempting answer because the work was done in a laboratory, but no gene was cut, changed or inserted: the whole existing set of genes was copied as it was.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is a product of the Krebs cycle?
g12-biology.e: Each turn of the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix strips hydrogen from the intermediates onto carriers, giving 3 NADH and 1 FADH2 , makes 1 ATP through GTP by substrate level phosphorylation, and releases 2 molecules of CO2 . Pyruvate is the tempting option, but pyruvate comes out of glycolysis and is the input that feeds the cycle, not a product of it. ​ ​

g12-biology.t:
In a metabolic pathway(A-->B-->C-->D) where each step is catalyzed by a separate enzyme which substance
in the pathway serves as an allosteric regulator?
g12-biology.e: In feedback inhibition of metabolic pathways, the end-product (Substance D) acts as an allosteric regulator (inhibitor) by binding to an allosteric site on the first enzyme.

g12-biology.t: Hummus & chimpanzees, both evolved from a common ancestor that lived about
g12-biology.e: Genetic and fossil evidence show that humans (misspelled as 'Hummus' in the stem) and chimpanzees diverged from a common ancestor approximately 6 million years ago.

g12-biology.t:
In an HIV/AIDS community screening, students were asked to take part in voluntary testing. The following
discussion presents the views of four grade 12 students named A, B, C and D towards HIV testing. Student A: I
should not take the testing; it is simply boring. Student B: We should take the testing, since we are educated;
we should be exemplary. Student C: If we get tested and got positive, what should we do? So, let us not get
tested. Student D: You know, this HIVIAIDS testing is simply a business. We should not be cheated. Which
student do you think is correct?
g12-biology.e: Student B shows a responsible and educated attitude towards HIV testing, recognizing the importance of being tested to set a positive example for the community.

g12-biology.t:
If certain food stuff gave a positive result with benedicts test only after it was hydrolysed with hydrochloric acid,
which of the following substances could it be?
g12-biology.e: Non-reducing sugars, such as sucrose, do not reduce Benedict's reagent directly; they yield a positive result only after being hydrolysed by an acid (such as HCl) into their constituent reducing monosaccharides.

g12-biology.t: Which part of the cell makes necessary changes packages and secretes proteins?
g12-biology.e: The Golgi apparatus modifies (e.g., glycosylation), sorts, packages, and directs proteins received from the rough endoplasmic reticulum for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following groups probably ate more of a herbivorous diet?
g12-biology.e: Australopithecus afarensis lived earlier and possessed dental adaptations (such as thick enamel and large molars) suited for grinding fibrous plant materials, eating a much higher proportion of vegetation than later Homo species. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Baby ostriches tend to follow the first moving object that they see as they hatch out of the eggs. What kind of
animal behaviour does this demonstrate?
g12-biology.e: This phenomenon describes imprinting, which is classified in the Ethiopian curriculum as a form of learned behavior that occurs during a critical, sensitive period early in an animal's life. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which of the following classes of molecule CANNOT pass easily across the cell membrane by simple diffusion?
g12-biology.e: The hydrophobic core of the lipid bilayer acts as a barrier to polar molecules, preventing them from easily crossing the membrane by simple diffusion.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following forms of nitrogen are readily utilization by green plants?
g12-biology.e: Although plants can absorb ammonium, nitrate (NO3-) is the primary, most abundant, and readily absorbed form of inorganic nitrogen utilized by green plants from the soil.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is responsible for the bending of a young plant towards a unidirectional source of light?
o: Increased rate of cell division on the light side
Faster growth rate on the dark side
Reduced auxin concentration on dark side
g12-biology.e: Phototropism is caused by auxins migrating to the shaded (dark) side of the shoot, stimulating cell elongation and resulting in a faster growth rate on the dark side, which bends the shoot toward the light.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following expression is more related to the phase "survival of the fittest"?
g12-biology.e: Herbert Spencer coined the phrase 'survival of the fittest,' which Charles Darwin later used interchangeably with his concept of natural selection.

g12-biology.t: Biological tool that is used to separate components of different molecular weight is known as;
g12-biology.e: A centrifuge is a laboratory device used to separate components of a mixture based on their size, shape, density, and molecular weight by spinning them at high speeds.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following paired organelle are membrane-bound?
g12-biology.e: Chloroplasts and mitochondria are each wrapped in a double membrane, and both also carry folded membranes inside, the thylakoids and the cristae, where their energy reactions take place. Ribosomes have no membrane at all: they are two blocks of RNA and protein, which is why every option pairing a ribosome with something else fails. Option A is the tempting one because a peroxisome is genuinely membrane bound, but its partner in that pair is the ribosome, so the pair as a whole is wrong. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following processes has a decreasing effect on the concentration of atmospheric carbon
dioxide?
g12-biology.e: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to produce organic compounds, while respiration, combustion, and decomposition all release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. (1)

g12-biology.t: Identify learned behavior from the following.
o: Child withdraws hand from hot things.
g12-biology.e: A dog trained to hunt represents a learned behavior because it is acquired through training and experience, unlike the innate behaviors listed in the other options.

g12-biology.t: During which stage of aerobic respiration dose oxidative phosphorylatuion occur?
g12-biology.e: Oxidative phosphorylation occurs via chemiosmosis, where ATP synthase utilizes the proton gradient established by the electron transport chain to phosphorylate ADP to ATP.

g12-biology.t: Which class of enzymes joins to molecule together by formation of new bonds?
g12-biology.e: Ligases are the class of enzymes that catalyze the joining (ligation) of two molecules accompanied by the hydrolysis of a high-energy phosphate bond (such as ATP).

g12-biology.t: Which group of organic compound includes the enzymes?
g12-biology.e: Enzymes are biological catalysts that are almost exclusively globular proteins.

g12-biology.t: Into which of the following organic compound can lipase maltase and sucrase be grouped?
g12-biology.e: Lipase, maltase, and sucrase are all enzymes, typically recognizable by the suffix '-ase', that catalyze the breakdown of lipids, maltose, and sucrose, respectively. (1)

g12-biology.t:
From evolutionary point of view, which of the following animals is expected to have haemoglobin proteins that
are least similar to that of human?
g12-biology.e: Frogs are amphibians, which diverged earliest from the evolutionary lineage leading to mammals, meaning their hemoglobin sequence has accumulated the most differences compared to humans.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following processes in the phosphate cycle DOES NOT return phosphate ions to the soil?
g12-biology.e: Cellular respiration is a process that releases carbon dioxide and water into the environment, playing a key role in the carbon and water cycles. It does not release or return phosphate ions to the soil, unlike weathering, fertilizer use, and decomposition.

g12-biology.t:
Among the following scientists who contributed to the cell theory, identify the one who stated that a cell can
arise only from another cell like it.
g12-biology.e: Rudolf Virchow added the third tenet to the cell theory with his principle 'Omnis cellula e cellula', stating that cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

g12-biology.t: What is the best term that expresses the movement of substances in cells against their concentration gradient?
g12-biology.e: Active transport moves molecules or ions across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient using energy, typically in the form of ATP.

g12-biology.t:
Which part of the digestive system is responsible for producing enzymes that digest carbohydrates, proteins,
and fats?
g12-biology.e: Pancreatic juice is the one secretion that carries all three enzyme classes at once: amylase for starch, trypsin and other proteases for protein, and lipase for fat. It empties into the duodenum through the pancreatic duct. The small intestine tempts because its lining does make enzymes such as maltase and peptidases, but those finish the job on small molecules rather than supply the full set.

g12-biology.t: Glycolysis occurs in the
g12-biology.e: Glycolysis takes place entirely within the cytoplasm (cytosol) of the cell and does not require membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following importance of water is directly related with its ideal viscosity?
g12-biology.e: Water has a relatively low viscosity, allowing it to flow easily through narrow tubes like blood vessels and xylem, making it an ideal transport medium.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following molecules can serve as a raw material for industries that produce glucose?
g12-biology.e: Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose monomers; industrial hydrolysis of starch yields glucose syrups.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following resources is needed by an ecosystem from outside in order to sustain itself
g12-biology.e: Unlike chemical nutrients, which cycle within ecosystems, energy cannot be recycled and must continuously enter the ecosystem from an external source, most commonly sunlight.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following stage of photosynthesis can take place in the dark?
g12-biology.e: The Calvin cycle represents the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis, utilizing ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide without the direct requirement of light.

g12-biology.t: Which group of archaebacterial are called salt loving bacteria?
g12-biology.e: Halophiles are specialized extremophilic archaebacteria that thrive in environments with very high salt concentrations.

g12-biology.t: Ammonium compounds are oxidized to nitrate by
g12-biology.e: Nitrifying bacteria, such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter, oxidize ammonia and ammonium compounds first to nitrites and then to nitrates during the nitrogen cycle.

g12-biology.t: What does an evolutionary selective pressure that acts around the mean do?
g12-biology.e: Natural selection that acts to favor the average phenotype and selects against extremes is known as stabilizing selection, so it stabilizes the population around the mean.

g12-biology.t: Which two groups of organisms does the fossil animal known as Archeopteryx link?
g12-biology.e: Archaeopteryx is a famous transitional fossil displaying a mix of reptilian features (such as teeth and a long bony tail) and avian features (such as feathers and wings), linking reptiles and birds.

g12-biology.t: From the following alternatives select the common features that are found both in animal and plant cells.
o: Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, chloroplast and Golgi apparatus
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, lysosome and Golgi apparatus
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, large vacuole and Golgi apparatus
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum
g12-biology.e: Animal and plant cells are both eukaryotic, so they share the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum. The wrong options each smuggle in a structure that belongs to only one cell type: chloroplasts and the single large vacuole are found in plant cells, while lysosomes are typical of animal cells.

g12-biology.t: In which of the following are flowers and fruits found?
g12-biology.e: Flowers and fruits are the defining features of the angiosperms, the flowering plants, and monocots and dicots are the two groups the angiosperms are divided into. The flower is the reproductive structure and the fruit is the ripened ovary that protects and spreads the seeds. Gymnosperms are the tempting answer because they also make seeds, but their seeds sit exposed on the scales of a cone, with no true flower and no fruit around them.

g12-biology.t:
If your body cannot make enough red blood cells, which one of the following mineral rich foods can correct this
problem?
g12-biology.e: Red blood cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin, and iron is the mineral at the centre of every haemoglobin molecule. When the body lacks iron it cannot make enough healthy red blood cells, a condition called anaemia, so iron rich foods correct the problem. Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland, calcium builds bones and teeth, and sodium balances body fluids; none of them builds red blood cells.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is different from the rest with regard to conservation of vegetation?
o: Replanting of land with endemic species
Large scale introduction of exotic plants
g12-biology.e: The large-scale introduction of exotic plants often threatens native biodiversity and ecosystems, unlike the other options which promote the conservation of native and endemic vegetation.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following tools is used by a biologist to study the internal anatomy of experimental animals?
g12-biology.e: A dissecting kit contains instruments such as scalpels, scissors, and forceps, which are essential for opening and exposing the internal anatomical structures of experimental animals.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following events is an example of a sex influenced trait?
g12-biology.e: Pattern baldness is a classic sex-influenced trait because its expression is dependent on hormone levels; the allele acts as a dominant trait in males but as a recessive trait in females.

g12-biology.t:
If organisms share very similar molecules such as DNA, then they must be closely related evolutionarily. Which
evidence of evolution supports the above information?
g12-biology.e: Comparing molecular structures, such as DNA, RNA, and proteins, to determine evolutionary relationships among different organisms falls under the field of comparative biochemistry.

g12-biology.t:
A plant cell is placed in a solution which has lower solute concentration than its contents. After a few minutes
the cell will become
g12-biology.e: When a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration than the cell contents), water enters the cell by osmosis, causing the vacuole to swell and push against the rigid cell wall, making the cell turgid.

g12-biology.t: In which organ of the human body are more bacteria found?
g12-biology.e: The human large intestine (colon) harbors the highest concentration and absolute number of bacteria of any organ in the body, forming the gut microbiota.

g12-biology.t: In Gram staining, if some bacteria retain the crystal violet after counter staining, then the bacteria is
g12-biology.e: Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan cell wall that successfully retains the crystal violet-iodine complex, even after alcohol decolorization and counterstaining, appearing purple.

g12-biology.t: Bacteria can cause diseases in all of the following mechanisms EXCEPT
o: entering living cells and disrupting metabolic systems.
invading and growing on the tissues of organs.
changing the genetic structure of host cells.
g12-biology.e: Changing the genetic structure of host cells is characteristic of viruses (like retroviruses), whereas bacteria cause disease by tissue invasion and releasing toxins, not by altering host DNA.

g12-biology.t: Among the following, which one had the cranial capacity of about the same size as that Of Homo sapiens?
g12-biology.e: The Neanderthal man had a cranial capacity of approximately 1400 to 1600 cc, which is highly comparable to, and sometimes slightly larger than, that of modern Homo sapiens (averaging ~1350-1400 cc).

g12-biology.t: All are correct about genetic fingerprinting except:
o: It is unique to individuals except identical twins
It is based on RNA analysis
It is made by gel electrophoresis in the PCR machine
It is used for crime investigation
g12-biology.e: Genetic fingerprinting compares DNA. Repeated sequences that vary from person to person are copied by PCR, cut, and separated by gel electrophoresis into a banding pattern that is unique except in identical twins. So the statement that it is based on RNA analysis is the false one. Option C is tempting because its wording is loose, but PCR and gel electrophoresis really are the tools used.

g12-biology.t: Which groups of lipids are bipolar due to the presence of hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions?
g12-biology.e: Phospholipids are amphipathic (bipolar) molecules consisting of a hydrophilic (polar) phosphate head and two hydrophobic (non-polar) fatty acid tails.

g12-biology.t:
If one base in the six triplets of the gene coding for one of the four polypeptides in the haemoglobin molecule
alters the triplet from GAG to GTG, which one of the following biological terms best describes the above
phenomenon?
g12-biology.e: A change in a single base pair of a DNA sequence (such as GAG to GTG in the beta-globin gene, which causes sickle-cell anemia) is defined as a point mutation.

g12-biology.t:
If a sample fruit juice and some drops of Benedict’s solution obtain a brick – red precipitate up on warming the
mixture, what does the juice contain?
g12-biology.e: Benedict's solution is a chemical reagent used to detect the presence of reducing sugars; a change to a brick-red precipitate upon heating indicates a high concentration of reducing sugars.

g12-biology.t: Aggregation of a large number of penguins staying close to each other to conserve heat can be an example of a
g12-biology.e: The cooperative huddling of penguins to conserve heat is a group interaction that enhances survival, which is a classic example of social behavior.

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following bacteria produces ammonium ion by forming a symbiotic association with peas and
beans?
g12-biology.e: Rhizobium is a symbiotic, nitrogen-fixing bacterium that inhabits the root nodules of legumes (such as peas and beans) and converts atmospheric nitrogen into ammonium ions.

g12-biology.t:
This item is based on the following course of human evolution.
1.Use of fire and other tools
2.Increase in brain size
3.Emergence of Homo sapiens
4.Bipedal walking and arboreal life
Which of the following is the correct order of the above evolutionary time line markers?
g12-biology.e: Walking upright on two legs (bipedalism) appeared first in human evolution, in early ancestors that were leaving arboreal (tree) life. Brain size then increased gradually over millions of years. With bigger brains, species such as Homo erectus began using fire and better tools. The emergence of our own species, Homo sapiens, came last. So the timeline is 4, 2, 1, 3.

g12-biology.t:
The allele for baldness is found on somatic chromosomes. But it is more expressed in males than females.
Consequently, it is taken as
g12-biology.e: Sex-influenced traits are determined by autosomal genes but are expressed differently in males and females due to hormonal differences, such as male pattern baldness being dominant in males but recessive in females.

g12-biology.t: What is the ultimate source of renege for all organism living on the earth?
g12-biology.e: The sun is the ultimate source of energy for life on Earth, captured by autotrophs via photosynthesis and passed through food webs.

g12-biology.t:
Which genus of bacteria oxidize hydrogen sulphide to sulphate and make sulphate ions available to be taken by
plant roots from the soil?
g12-biology.e: Thiobacillus species are chemolithotrophic bacteria that obtain energy by oxidizing sulfur and hydrogen sulfide into sulfate, making it available for uptake by plant roots.

g12-biology.t:
This item is based on the following choices of feeding habit employed by organisms.
I. Using nutrients dissolved in the surrounding medium
II. Manufacturing own nutrients by photosynthesis
III. Depending on other plants or animals for food
Which method/s the protozoan used to get their nutrition? They employed
g12-biology.e: Protozoa as a group use all three feeding methods. Saprozoic protozoa absorb nutrients dissolved in the water around them (I). Plant like protozoa such as Euglena carry chloroplasts and make food by photosynthesis (II). Holozoic and parasitic protozoa, such as Amoeba and Plasmodium, feed on other organisms (III). Because different members use different methods, the full answer is I, II and III.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following chromosomal errors creates a cell with an extra chromosome?
g12-biology.e: Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division, resulting in daughter cells with an abnormal number of chromosomes (such as an extra chromosome).

g12-biology.t: What triggers fermentation during exercise?
o: Production of ATP beyond the cells demand
g12-biology.e: During strenuous exercise, oxygen supply to muscle tissues cannot keep up with the high demand, leading to a shortage of oxygen and triggering lactic acid fermentation to regenerate NAD+ and sustain glycolysis.

g12-biology.t: The most complex structure of proteins is called
g12-biology.e: Quaternary structure is the highest and most complex level of protein organization, formed when two or more polypeptide chains interact to form a functional multimeric protein.

g12-biology.t: In all the following condition diffusion is faster except;
g12-biology.e: The rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the distance; thus, diffusion is extremely slow over long distances, which is why multicellular organisms require circulatory systems.

g12-biology.t:
Regarding human evolution, which hominid was unable to run faster and had small brain size as compared to
the others?
g12-biology.e: Homo habilis is the earliest and most primitive species of the genus Homo listed; it possessed a significantly smaller brain size (around 600-700 cc) and lacked the anatomical adaptations for endurance running found in Homo erectus.

g12-biology.t: An organic molecule which is an important part of structure of chromosome is
g12-biology.e: Chromosomes are made of DNA coiled around histone proteins. Proteins are polymers composed of amino acid monomers, making amino acids a vital structural component of chromosomes.

g12-biology.t: Which type of animal behavior happens with out learning?
g12-biology.e: Innate behavior is genetically programmed and inherited, allowing an animal to perform it correctly the first time without prior experience or learning.

g12-biology.t: The molecule of which pigment is located at the reaction center of a photosystem?
g12-biology.e: The reaction center of a photosystem contains a specialized pair of chlorophyll a molecules that donate energized electrons to the primary electron acceptor.

g12-biology.t: Both photosynthesis and respiration are involved in:
g12-biology.e: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to make organic compounds, while respiration breaks these compounds down to release carbon dioxide back, making both vital to the carbon cycle.

g12-biology.t: The behavior which trainers look, if modified, could lead to the desired behavior and reward such a behavior is
g12-biology.e: An operant is a behavior that is actively emitted by an organism and operates on the environment; in training, operant behaviors are reinforced with rewards to shape the desired outcome.

g12-biology.t: Which process produced mRNA during protein synthesis?
g12-biology.e: Transcription is the process by which a specific segment of DNA is copied into messenger RNA (mRNA) by RNA polymerase.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following organelles settles out last when homogenized cells are centrifuged?
g12-biology.e: In differential centrifugation, the largest and densest components (nuclei) pellet first at low speeds, while the smallest components like ribosomes require the highest speeds and pellet last.

g12-biology.t: The evolution of species which is based upon the sum total adaptation changes could be preserved by:
g12-biology.e: Natural selection acts to preserve favorable adaptive variations in a population across generations while weeding out disadvantageous traits.

g12-biology.t:
In an experiment to study photosynthesis, a plant was provided with radioactive carbon dioxide as a metabolic
tracer and the radioactive carbon was incorporated first into oxaloacetate. Which one of the following would
best characterize this plant?
g12-biology.e: C4 plants use the enzyme PEP carboxylase to initially fix carbon dioxide into a 4-carbon compound, oxaloacetate, in the mesophyll cells.

g12-biology.t: How many fatty acids would a cell need to form a molecule of triglyceride
g12-biology.e: A triglyceride (triacylglycerol) is synthesized by esterifying three fatty acid chains to a single molecule of glycerol.

g12-biology.t: A chimpanzee concentrates to reach at a bunch of grapes hanging above its head. What kind of behavior is this?
g12-biology.e: Insight learning involves solving a problem rapidly by understanding the relationships between various parts of the problem without trial-and-error, as famously demonstrated by primates solving tasks to reach food.

g12-biology.t:
Consider the following chemical reaction below. RH2 + A E R + AH2 Based on the above chemical
reaction, in which classes of enzymes can enzyme "E" be grouped?
​
g12-biology.e: The chemical equation depicts a redox (oxidation-reduction) reaction in which hydrogen is transferred, which is catalyzed by enzymes belonging to the class oxidoreductases.

g12-biology.t:
Some amino acids are synthesized using transamination process in the cell. This activity more describes the
cell's
g12-biology.e: Anabolism refers to metabolic pathways that construct molecules from smaller units, requiring energy; the biosynthesis of amino acids through transamination is an anabolic process.

g12-biology.t: The total amount of living tissue within a given trophic level is called:
g12-biology.e: Biomass is defined as the total mass of living organic matter within a specific trophic level or given ecosystem.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following groups of viruses copy their RNA to DNA?
g12-biology.e: Retroviruses possess an RNA genome and use the enzyme reverse transcriptase to transcribe their RNA into DNA inside the host cell.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following laboratory glassware is used for culturing bacteria?
g12-biology.e: A Petri dish containing nutrient agar is the standard laboratory equipment used for culturing microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is NOT the correct characteristics of tropical rainforests?
g12-biology.e: Tropical rainforests are recognized as having the highest terrestrial biodiversity on Earth, so possessing low biodiversity is incorrect.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is an example of anthropogenic driving factor that contributes to species extinction?
g12-biology.e: Anthropogenic means caused by human beings. Expanding farmland is a human activity that clears forests and grasslands, destroying the habitats that species need, so it is an anthropogenic driver of extinction. Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and natural wildfires happen without human action, so they are natural drivers.

g12-biology.t:
For a biological detergent to effectively remove oily and greasy dirt, which of the following enzymes should it
contain?
g12-biology.e: Lipases are enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of fats and oils (lipids), making them ideal for removing greasy stains in biological detergents.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following is not practice that affects reproductive health?
g12-biology.e: The question asks which practice does not damage reproductive health. Planning the gap between births lets the mother recover and improves the health of both mother and child, so it protects health rather than harming it. Early marriage is the tempting distractor because it is common, but it exposes a girl to pregnancy before her body is ready and raises the risk of obstructed labour and fistula.

g12-biology.t:
Which organic molecules are formed when two fatty acid molecules are bounded to the glycerol and the place
of the third is taken by a phosphate group?
g12-biology.e: Phospholipids are lipids containing a glycerol backbone bound to two fatty acids and a phosphate group, forming a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails.

g12-biology.t: All of the following features define a chromosome EXCEPT
o: made up of DNA and protein.
exists in pairs in diploid organisms.
contains hundreds to thousands of genes.
g12-biology.e: The functional unit of inheritance is the gene, not the chromosome. A chromosome is a much larger structure made of DNA wound around proteins, it carries hundreds to thousands of genes, and in diploid organisms chromosomes come in homologous pairs. So statements A, B and C describe a chromosome, while D describes a gene.

g12-biology.t:
When two species are compared ,which of the following sources of evidence is least informative about the
degree of relationships between the species?
g12-biology.e: A polysaccharide such as starch or cellulose is the same sugar, glucose, repeated over and over. Because the units do not vary, there is no sequence to compare between two species, so the molecule carries almost no information about how closely they are related. The amino acid sequence of proteins is the tempting answer because it is also a comparison of building blocks, but there are twenty different amino acids, so their order differs between species and the number of differences measures how far apart the species are.

g12-biology.t: Organelles in the cytoplasm that are known as 'power house' of the cell are:
g12-biology.e: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through aerobic respiration.

g12-biology.t:
Currently, natural resources are being depleted at increasing rate and waste materials are accumulated and
discharged freely into water bodies. What is the best strategy to overcome these problems?
g12-biology.e: Recycling reduces the demand for raw natural resource extraction and diverts waste materials from landfill and water body dumping back into productive use.

g12-biology.t:
What is the method of conservation in which animals are kept in captivity and plants are grown in botanical
gardens?
g12-biology.e: Ex-situ conservation refers to the preservation of components of biological diversity outside their natural habitats, such as in zoos, botanical gardens, and seed banks.

g12-biology.t:
Which filed studies the way in which individual traits of organisms are transmitted from one generation to the
next?
g12-biology.e: Genetics is the branch of biology that deals with heredity, specifically how traits are passed down from parents to offspring across generations. (1)

g12-biology.t: What is the main function of the cell membrane? It controls
g12-biology.e: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, so its primary function is to control the transport of molecules into and out of the cell. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Suppose a hypothetical cube- shaped cell has sides of 10 micrometers, what is the surface area to volume ratio
of this cell?
g12-biology.e: For a cube of side s = 10 μm, the total surface area is 6 × s^2 = 600 μm^2 and the volume is s^3 = 1000 μm^3. The ratio of surface area to volume is 600:1000, which simplifies to 6:10.

g12-biology.t:
A biologist is organizing a museum exhibit and wants to categorize four research scientists based on the
specific groups of organisms they study. Scientist A: Studies the structure, function of animals. Scientist B:
Focuses on the scientific study of plants, their physiology and genetics. Scientist C: Investigates the complex
world of insects. Based on these descriptions, Scientists A, B, C can be classified under which biology subfields, respectively?
g12-biology.e: The sub-fields are named after what they study. Zoology is the study of animals, botany is the study of plants, and entomology is the study of insects. Scientist A studies animals, B studies plants and C studies insects, so the order is zoology, botany, entomology. Option B is tempting because it holds the same three words, but it puts botany with the animal researcher and zoology with the plant researcher.

g12-biology.t: The process in which individuals with a particular heritable trait survive better than the other is
g12-biology.e: Natural selection is the process by which individuals with favorable, heritable traits are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing those advantageous traits on to the next generation.

g12-biology.t: Who conducted the famous experiment in 1953 that simulated early Earth conditions to test the origins of life?
g12-biology.e: In 1953 Stanley Miller, working with Harold Urey, sealed methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour in glassware and passed electric sparks through the mixture to imitate lightning on the early Earth. Amino acids appeared within days, which showed that the building blocks of life can form from simple gases with no living thing involved. Option B is the closest trap, because Oparin proposed the chemical origin hypothesis in the 1920s, but he did not run this experiment.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following behavioral biologists is known for his study about imprinting behavior in animals?
g12-biology.e: Konrad Lorenz is renowned for his ethological studies demonstrating imprinting behavior in newly hatched greylag geese.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following structures is NOT present in animal cells?
g12-biology.e: Animal cells are surrounded only by a flexible plasma membrane and lack a rigid cell wall, which is characteristic of plants, fungi, and bacteria.

g12-biology.t: "Skinner box" is used for experiments in:
g12-biology.e: The Skinner box, or operant conditioning chamber, is used to study animal behavior by training them to perform actions (like pressing a lever) in response to rewards or punishments.

g12-biology.t: Which molecule in the cell is the constituent of the gene?
g12-biology.e: Genes are specific functional segments of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), which is a type of nucleic acid.

g12-biology.t:
The organelle of the cell which is concerned with the synthesis of lipids in addition to being associated with
carbohydrate metabolism and detoxification is:
g12-biology.e: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is specialized for lipid and steroid synthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, calcium storage, and the detoxification of drugs and poisons.

g12-biology.t: Ethiopian Biological research center which is involved in mechanized farming is:
g12-biology.e: EIAR is the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research. It works on crops, livestock, soils and farm machinery, which is why mechanized farming falls under it. IBC is the tempting answer because it also deals with plants, but its job is conserving genetic resources and ecosystems, not farm technology.

g12-biology.t:
If a phagocytic white blood cell is unable to digest bacteria that have been engulfed, which organelles could be
failed to do this function?
g12-biology.e: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that fuse with phagosomes to digest engulfed pathogens; if lysosomes fail to function, the phagocytic cell cannot digest the bacteria.

g12-biology.t: In which area of enzyme application is invertase injected to sucrose paste in order to produce liquid chocolates?
g12-biology.e: Invertase hydrolyzes sucrose into glucose and fructose, creating a soft or liquid centre in chocolates, which is a major application in the food processing industry. (1)

g12-biology.t:
If radioactive substance that weighs one kilogram has a half-life of 100 years what would be the percentage of
the substance left after 300 years?
g12-biology.e: With a half-life of 100 years, 300 years corresponds to 3 half-lives. The remaining fraction is (1/2)^3 = 1/8, which equals 12.5% of the original substance.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following protozoan disease causes blindness, mental retardation & multi system organ familiarity?
g12-biology.e: Toxoplasmosis, caused by the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, can cause congenital infections leading to severe issues like blindness, mental retardation, and systemic organ damage.

g12-biology.t: Mutations become more serious and threatening if they occur on genes that regulate
g12-biology.e: Mutations in genes that regulate cell division (such as proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes) can lead to uncontrolled cell division and cancer, making them highly life-threatening.

g12-biology.t: What is a key threat of biodiversity in Ethiopia?
g12-biology.e: Climate change and desertification present major environmental challenges and significant threats to the rich biodiversity of Ethiopia.

g12-biology.t: Which class of HIV anti-retroviral drugs binds to T-cells in order to inhibit joining of the virus with its receptor?
g12-biology.e: Entry inhibitors (such as CCR5 antagonists) block HIV from entering host T-cells by binding to receptors on the T-cell surface, thereby preventing the viral envelope from attaching to its target.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is an ecosystem
o: The non-living components of an environment
All the organisms in a given area
g12-biology.e: An ecosystem is all the living things in an area together with the non living surroundings they depend on, and the flow of energy and nutrients between the two. A tropical rain forest fits this: it has its plants and animals plus the soil, water, air and sunlight they live in. Option C is the tempting answer, but all the organisms in an area with the physical surroundings left out is a community, which is only one half of an ecosystem.

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following external factors influence the turnover rate of enzymes by completely damaging their
tertiary structure?
g12-biology.e: Extremes in temperature and pH cause the denaturation of enzymes by disrupting the non-covalent bonds (such as hydrogen and ionic bonds) that maintain their tertiary structure, permanently destroying their activity.

g12-biology.t:
What is the processes called when two bacteria directly contact cell to cell and exchange their genetic
information?
g12-biology.e: Bacterial conjugation involves direct cell-to-cell contact through a sex pilus to transfer genetic material (such as a plasmid) from a donor to a recipient bacterium.

g12-biology.t:
To which of the following groups do those bacterio phages that integrate their DNA in to the chromosome of
their bacterial host belong?
g12-biology.e: A lysogenic phage does not destroy its host at once. It inserts its DNA into the bacterial chromosome as a prophage, which is then copied along with the host DNA every time the bacterium divides, and only later may it leave and start destroying cells. Lytic viruses are the tempting answer because they are the other half of the same story, but a lytic phage copies itself straight away and bursts the cell without ever joining the host chromosome. (1)

g12-biology.t: The structure of specimens can be studied after they are freshly collected using a
g12-biology.e: A field microscope is a portable microscope designed for use outdoors, allowing biologists to examine the microscopic structure of freshly collected specimens directly at the field site.

g12-biology.t: If a homogenate of eukaryotic cells is spun in a centrifuge, which of the cellular organelles settles out first?
g12-biology.e: The nucleus is the largest and densest organelle in eukaryotic cells; therefore, it precipitates out first at the lowest centrifugal speeds during differential centrifugation. (1)

g12-biology.t: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.
g12-biology.e: Professor Tilahun Yilma is a highly distinguished Ethiopian virologist who successfully developed a recombinant vaccine against rinderpest, a devastating viral disease of cattle.

g12-biology.t: Which theory proposes the origin of life to be from resistant spores landing on Earth from outer space?
g12-biology.e: The Cosmozoan theory (also known as the Panspermia theory) proposes that life on Earth originated from resistant spores or microorganisms that arrived from outer space.

g12-biology.t:
Suppose sites A,B,C and D have Simpson's Index of Diversity (d) values of 20,8,16,and 3, respectively, which site
is dominated by one or just a few species?
g12-biology.e: In Simpson's reciprocal index of diversity, higher values indicate high species richness and evenness, whereas low values (the minimum being 1) indicate a community dominated by only one or a few species; Site D has the lowest index (3).

g12-biology.t: The word science comes from the Latin word 'Scientia' meaning what ?
g12-biology.e: The word science is derived from the Latin noun 'scientia', which means 'knowledge'.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is classified as a mechanical measure of soil and water conservation?
g12-biology.e: Mechanical, or physical, conservation measures are structures that are built on the land to slow water down and hold soil in place. Check dams across gullies and terraces across a slope both do that, so they are mechanical measures. Planting tree seedlings is the tempting answer because it also protects soil, but living cover is a biological measure, and the Green Legacy initiative and area enclosure fall in the same biological group.

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following is correct if a molecule is transported across the plasma membrane using active
transport involving a carrier protein? The molecule is
g12-biology.e: Polar and charged molecules are hydrophilic and cannot easily pass through the hydrophobic lipid bilayer by simple diffusion; hence, they require carrier proteins for active transport against their concentration gradient. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following terms refers to the failure of sister chromatids to separate from one another during
anaphase?
g12-biology.e: Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division, leading to daughter cells with abnormal numbers of chromosomes.

g12-biology.t:
One of the following sources of evidence provides a more direct support to the process of Charles Darwin's
theory of evolution.
g12-biology.e: The study of the geographical distribution of organisms (biogeography) was one of the most compelling and direct fields of evidence that led Charles Darwin to formulate his theory of evolution.

g12-biology.t:
Gardener brings an ornamental plant from other country and plant it in urban parks. This species through time
moved into conservation area and caused a loss for many other plant species. This is a loss of biodiversity due to
g12-biology.e: When a non-native species is introduced and outcompetes native species, it is classified as an invasive species, causing biodiversity loss.

g12-biology.t: from among the following choice the field which is a branch or a part of biotechnology.
g12-biology.e: Genetic engineering is the core branch and tool of modern biotechnology, involving direct manipulation of an organism's genes.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following processes involved in the water cycle is carried out by green plants?
g12-biology.e: Transpiration is the process by which moisture is carried through plants from roots to small pores on leaves, where it changes to vapor and is released to the atmosphere.

g12-biology.t: The amount of energy required to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius is
g12-biology.e: Specific heat capacity is defined as the energy required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of a substance by 1°C. (1)

g12-biology.t: The scientific name of a house fly is:
g12-biology.e: The scientific binomial name of the common house fly is Musca domestica.

g12-biology.t: In which industrial products is pyruvate fermentation by yeast practically applied?
g12-biology.e: Brewing beer utilizes alcoholic fermentation by yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) to convert sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

g12-biology.t:
The terrestrial biome characterized by cold temperature, dry precipitation, frozen soil and inhabited by migrating
birds is
g12-biology.e: The tundra biome is characterized by very cold and dry conditions, permanently frozen soil (permafrost), and serves as a summer nesting ground for many migratory birds. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following is adaptation mechanism of animal in cold climate?
g12-biology.e: Blubber is a thick layer of fat under the skin. Fat conducts heat poorly, so it holds body heat inside the animal and keeps it warm in cold water or cold air. Large thin ears is the opposite adaptation. A wide, thin ear carries a lot of blood close to the air and loses heat, which suits a desert animal such as a fox, not a polar one.

g12-biology.t:
Grade 12 students went to a field and collected plant specimens for identification in the laboratory. They wanted
to preserve the plant parts for some times and specimens can be analyzed later. Which one of the following
biological tool is used for their activities?
g12-biology.e: A plant press is a biological tool used to flatten, dry, and preserve plant specimens collected in the field for long-term laboratory identification and study. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by mosquitoes?
g12-biology.e: Malaria is a vector-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted to humans via the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. (1)

g12-biology.t:
At which stage of the population growth curve is the rate of natality and the rate of mortality expected to be
equal?
g12-biology.e: In the stationary phase of a population growth curve, the carrying capacity is reached, and the rate of natality (births) equals the rate of mortality (deaths), resulting in a stable population size.

g12-biology.t:
78. Which of the following involve extracting and obtaining energy from their environment by enzyme mediated
chemical reaction?
g12-biology.e: Metabolism, which involves extracting and obtaining energy from the environment through enzyme-mediated chemical reactions, is a defining characteristic of all living things.

g12-biology.t:
Consider the following reaction: Reactant A + Reactant B → Enzyme → Intermediate → Product AB + Enzyme? At 
which point are the chemical bonds weakened?
g12-biology.e: During an enzyme-catalyzed reaction, the chemical bonds of the substrates are weakened and strained while in the intermediate enzyme-substrate complex, reducing the activation energy required for the reaction.

g12-biology.t: Which physiological response helps conserve heat when the core body temperature drops?
g12-biology.e: When the core cools, the arterioles supplying the skin narrow. Less warm blood reaches the surface, so less heat is radiated away and the core is protected. Vasodilation is the tempting opposite: it widens those vessels, floods the skin with blood and increases heat loss, which is what the body does when it is too hot.

g12-biology.t: Why do we get tired and fatigued during heavy exercise such as long distance running? It is due to
g12-biology.e: During intense exercise, oxygen supply to muscles is limited, causing them to undergo anaerobic respiration. This leads to the accumulation of lactic acid, which causes muscle fatigue and soreness.

g12-biology.t:
Which property of water is useful for life that it continues in relatively warm water underneath through the cold
weather?
o: High density in its solid form than its liquid form
g12-biology.e: High specific heat capacity allows water to resist rapid temperature changes, keeping the water underneath relatively warm and stable for aquatic life during cold weather. Option B is factually incorrect because solid water (ice) is actually less dense than liquid water, which is why it floats.

g12-biology.t: From which of the following do scientists usually formulate a hypothesis?
g12-biology.e: The scientific method typically starts with observations, from which scientists formulate a testable hypothesis to explain those observations.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following enzymes has its optimum pH within low pH range?
g12-biology.e: Pepsin is an enzyme found in the stomach that functions best in a highly acidic environment, with an optimum pH of about 1.5 to 2.0.

g12-biology.t: Which part of the human elementary canal contains digestive enzymes that function at acidic pH?
g12-biology.e: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid along with pepsinogen, creating an acidic environment (pH ~1.5–2) necessary for pepsin to digest proteins effectively. (1)

g12-biology.t: Which element is found in nucleic acids?
g12-biology.e: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are composed of nucleotides, which contain a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group containing phosphorus.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following is the basic characteristic of mutation? It is
g12-biology.e: Mutations are primary sources of genetic variation and are characterized as spontaneous, random, and unpredictable changes in the genome.

g12-biology.t: Which one of the following cellular forms did Robert Hooke observe under his crude microscope?
g12-biology.e: In 1665, Robert Hooke examined thin slices of non-living bottle cork and observed small, box-like compartments that were actually the empty cell walls of dead plant cells.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following parts of plant roots is harboring nitrogen fixing bacteria
g12-biology.e: Root nodules, found primarily on the roots of leguminous plants, house symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Rhizobium.

g12-biology.t: Among the vertebrate found In ethiopia, which class has the highest percentage of endemic species?
g12-biology.e: Amphibians have the highest rate of endemism among Ethiopian vertebrates, with around 40–50% of known species being endemic to the country.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following laboratory tools is LEAST accurate to measure 1 ml of liquid?
g12-biology.e: Beakers have wide diameters and approximate graduations, making them the least accurate laboratory glassware for measuring small volumes such as 1 ml. (1)

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following techniques is employed in the transfer of human insulin gene to bacteria inorder to
produce human insulin in the bacteria?
g12-biology.e: Recombinant DNA technique is used to splice the human insulin gene into bacterial plasmids, allowing the genetically modified bacteria to synthesize human insulin. (1)

g12-biology.t: In the case of enzymatic chemical reactions, what do you call the substance that is acted up on by an enzyme?
g12-biology.e: The reactant or chemical substance upon which an enzyme acts and binds at its active site is called the substrate.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following cell types can be rich in lysosomes?
g12-biology.e: Phagocytic white blood cells swallow bacteria and cell debris into a vesicle, and lysosomes then fuse with that vesicle and empty their digestive enzymes onto the contents. A cell that does this all day needs a large stock of lysosomes ready to use. Nerve cells are the tempting answer because they are large and busy, but their work is carrying electrical signals, so they have no reason to hold a store of digestive enzymes.

g12-biology.t:
Traditional fermentation products such as 'Tella' and 'Injera', and modern industrial products such as detergents
and textiles generally would not have been possible without the use of
g12-biology.e: Both traditional fermentation (using yeasts and bacteria) and modern industrial processes like textile and detergent manufacturing rely on enzymes to catalyze chemical reactions.

g12-biology.t: What is the natural process that allows continuity of supply of nutrients to organisms in an ecosystem?
g12-biology.e: Nutrient recycling (biogeochemical cycling) ensures that essential elements like carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus are continuously cycled through the ecosystem, maintaining a constant supply for living organisms.

g12-biology.t: The evolutionary process that allows survival of well adapted and successfully reproducing individuals is called
g12-biology.e: Natural selection is the evolutionary mechanism where individuals with favorable, heritable traits are more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass those adaptive traits to the next generation.

g12-biology.t:
Which one of the following is the result of the similarity observed between the wings of a bird and a
pterodactyl?
g12-biology.e: The wings of birds and pterodactyls are analogous structures that arose independently through convergent evolution to serve the function of flight.

g12-biology.t: During alcohol fermentation pyruvic acid in the presence of pyruvate decarboxylase is first converted to .
g12-biology.e: In alcoholic fermentation, pyruvate decarboxylase first removes a carboxyl group from pyruvic acid to form acetaldehyde and carbon dioxide, which is then reduced to ethanol.

g12-biology.t:
Which kind of enzyme inhibitors bind to enzyme only weakly and the bond that hold them breaks easily
releasing the inhibitor to allow the enzyme to become active again?
o: Inhibitors that permanently alter enzyme structure
Inhibitors that bind strongly to enzymes
g12-biology.e: Reversible inhibitors bind to enzymes through non-covalent, weak interactions that can readily dissociate, allowing the enzyme to regain activity.

g12-biology.t:
Which of the following mechanism moves digested amino acids and glucose across the plasma membrane of
the cell lining the wall of the small intestine?
g12-biology.e: Absorption of glucose and amino acids from the intestinal lumen into the epithelial cells occurs via active transport, primarily using sodium-dependent cotransporters.

g12-biology.t: 69. Which of the following absorb different wavelength of light?
g12-biology.e: Photosynthetic pigments, such as chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and carotenoids, are specialized molecules that absorb specific wavelengths of light to drive the process of photosynthesis.

g12-biology.t: Which of the following is NOT usually true as an ecological succession progresses to advanced seral stages ?
o: The depth of the soil increase
g12-biology.e: As succession advances the habitat gets richer, not poorer. Soil deepens, more kinds of plants and animals arrive, more niches open up and the amount of life the area can support goes up, so saying less population is supported is the statement that is not true. Deeper soil is the tempting answer if the question is read too fast, but soil building is exactly what the earlier stages do for the later ones, so that statement is true and is not what the question asks for.

g12-biology.t: Homologus structures are evidence of evolution produced from:
g12-biology.e: Homologous structures share a common evolutionary origin but have different functions, which is key evidence for evolution studied under comparative anatomy.

g12-biology.t:
74. In the calvin cycle which of the following compound is produced in C3 plants first?
​
g12-biology.e: In C3 plants, the first stable product of carbon fixation is 3-phosphoglycerate (PGA), which is subsequently reduced to Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P) during the Calvin cycle. Since PGA is not listed, G3P represents the most immediate Calvin cycle product among the options. (1)

g12-chemistry.t:
Which of the following process involves preventing the growth of bacteria, fungi and reducing the oxidation of
fats?
g12-chemistry.e: Food preservation involves methods that inhibit microbial growth (bacteria, fungi) and retard the oxidation of fats to prevent spoilage and maintain food quality.

g12-chemistry.t: Which of the following is used in the reaction called saponification?
g12-chemistry.e: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils using a strong base such as NaOH or KOH to produce soap and glycerol.

g12-chemistry.t:
Which substance is used to lower the melting point of aluminum oxide ore in the electrolytic extraction of
aluminum?
g12-chemistry.e: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to alumina (Al₂O₃) to lower its melting point from about 2050°C to around 950°C, making the electrolytic extraction of aluminum energy-efficient.

g12-chemistry.t: Which one of the following fertilizers supplies the highest percentage of nitrogen to plants?
g12-chemistry.e: Urea, CO(NH2)2, has a molar mass of 60 g/mol and contains 28 g/mol of nitrogen, translating to approximately 46.7% nitrogen, which is the highest among the choices.

g12-chemistry.t: All of the following compounds contain ionic and covalent bonds except:
g12-chemistry.e: In N H4 Cl, CaCO3 and N a3 P O4 a polyatomic ion is held together inside by covalent bonds, and that ion is held to its partner ion by an ionic bond, so each has both bond types. In H3 N -BF3 the nitrogen donates its lone pair to boron, which is a dative covalent bond, and no ions are formed at all. A is tempting because ammonium looks like a molecule, but N H4+ and Cl− are separate ions. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​

g12-chemistry.t:
The shift in the position of equilibrium caused by the addition of an ion already involved in the reaction is known
as _________.
g12-chemistry.e: The common-ion effect is the reduction in solubility or shift in equilibrium when an ionic compound containing an ion already present in the solution is added.

g12-chemistry.t: The species that being reduced and causes oxidation is a/an
g12-chemistry.e: An oxidizing agent is the reactant that oxidizes another substance by gaining electrons, meaning the oxidizing agent itself is reduced in the process.

g12-chemistry.t: What property of an ionic compound can be investigated by heating it in a crucible?
g12-chemistry.e: Heating an ionic compound in a crucible allows one to observe the temperature at which it transitions from a solid to a liquid, which determines its melting point.

g12-chemistry.t: The process of vulcanization of rubber makes it
g12-chemistry.e: Vulcanization involves cross-linking polymer chains of rubber with sulfur, which makes the rubber harder, stiffer, and more resistant to heat and wear.

g12-chemistry.t:
A student added 25 mL of AgNO 3 solution to a beaker and weighed the mass of the beaker and its content as
m 1 . He/she added 50 mL of a saturated solution of NaCl into the second beaker and weighed the mass of the
beaker and its content as m 2 . Finally, he/she mixed the two solutions and weighed the mass of the resulting
solution with the two beakers and recorded as m 3 . If he/she found that m 1 = m 2 , which one of the following
laws is investigated by this trial?
g12-chemistry.e: Comparing the total mass of reactants before a reaction and the total mass of products after the reaction is the classic experimental method to demonstrate the Law of Conservation of Mass.

g12-chemistry.t: Which of the following has the same number of significant figures as the number 1.00310?
g12-chemistry.e: The number 1.00310 has 6 significant figures. Among the choices, 199.791 also contains exactly 6 significant figures, while option A and B have 1, and option D has 4.

g12-chemistry.t:
​
​
The general formula for saturated monocarboxylic acids is
g12-chemistry.e: Saturated monocarboxylic acids (also known as alkanoic acids) contain one carboxyl group (-COOH) attached to an alkyl group, represented by the general formula RCOOH.

g12-chemistry.t:
Which of the four colligative properties arises in systems where there is an equilibrium between a liquid solution
phase and a second liquid phase?
g12-chemistry.e: Osmotic pressure involves an equilibrium established between two liquid phases (the pure solvent and the solution) across a semipermeable membrane.

g12-chemistry.t:
Aluminum reacts with a certain nonmetallic element, X to form a compound with the general formula AlX.
Element X is a diatomic gas at room temperature. Element X must be
g12-chemistry.e: Aluminum has a +3 oxidation state, so for the neutral 1:1 compound AlX, X must have a -3 oxidation state. Nitrogen (N) is a diatomic gas (N2) at room temperature and typically forms a -3 nitride ion, yielding AlN.

g12-chemistry.t:
A chemical bond that results from the attractive force between shared electrons and nonmetal nucleus is called
_____.
g12-chemistry.e: A covalent bond is formed by the electrostatic attraction between the shared pair of electrons and the positively charged nuclei of the nonmetal atoms. (1)

g12-chemistry.t:
A system does 15 J of work and no other changes take place. Which of the following function has fallen by 15
J?
g12-chemistry.e: According to the First Law of Thermodynamics (delta U = q + w), if a system does 15 J of work (w = -15 J) and no heat is exchanged (q = 0), its internal energy falls by 15 J.

g12-chemistry.t: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?
o: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions
Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements
Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine
g12-chemistry.e: Dalton's postulate that atoms are indivisible and indestructible was modified by modern atomic theory following the discovery of subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, and electrons).

g12-chemistry.t:
Given the following unbalanced equation KMnO4 + KI + H2 SO4 → K2 SO4 + MnSO4 + I2 + H2 O
How many grams of KMnO4 are needed to make 250 mL of 0.20 N solution?
​
​
​
​
​
​
​
​
