g12-civics.e: Citizenship acquired through parentage or descent, regardless of the country of birth, is known as jus sanguinis (right of blood). (1)

g12-civics.t: In most countries the term "government benefits" are related to,
g12-civics.e: Government benefits typically refer to public assistance and social welfare provisions such as healthcare, education, social security, and subsidies intended to improve the well-being of citizens.

g12-civics.t: Which of the following is important characteristics for effective civic participation?
o: Home base political organization and political agenda.
Focus on individual talent and competence.
g12-civics.e: Commitment and dedication to public welfare are core civic virtues that ensure meaningful and sustained civic participation.

g12-civics.t: Which of the following countries is unique example in the world that does not have a written constitution?
g12-civics.e: England (the United Kingdom) is the classic global example of a nation with an unwritten (uncodified) constitution, relying instead on statutes, common law, and conventions.

g12-civics.t:
Ato Kinde is a resident in Addis Ababa who is engaged in a retail business sector. He complained to the Wereda
Income and Revenue Authority that he is requested to pay more amount of tax than those who have the same
amount of earning with him. Accordingly, which principle of taxation is violated by the Wereda Income and
Revenue Authority in this case?
g12-civics.e: Horizontal equity is a principle of taxation which states that taxpayers with the same income or wealth should pay the same amount of tax. In this case, requesting Ato Kinde to pay more than others with the same earnings directly violates this principle.

g12-civics.t:
An individual who has claimed the right to refuse to perform active military service on the grounds of freedom of 
thought, conscience, or religion is referred to as
g12-civics.e: A conscientious objector is an individual who refuses to engage in military service or combat due to deeply held moral, ethical, or religious beliefs.

g12-civics.t:
According to the current Constitution of FDRE elected officials are given their power by the citizen of the
country. Which of the following basic principles of the Constitution is reflected by this practice?
o: Respect of human and democratic rights.
g12-civics.e: The constitutional principle where elected officials derive their mandate and authority from the citizens reflects the sovereignty of the people, as stated in Article 8 of the FDRE Constitution.

g12-civics.t: A lawful gathering of people to protest ,support or create awareness on a certain issue implies ;
g12-civics.e: A demonstration is people assembling in public to show support, to protest or to draw attention to an issue, and doing it within the law makes it peaceful. Article 30 of the FDRE Constitution protects that right. Popular participation is tempting because a demonstration is one form of it, but popular participation is the wide term covering voting, meetings and civic work, while the gathering described has its own name.

g12-civics.t: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of poverty?
o: Existence of a high infant mortality rate in a country.
A high average life expectancy and a high literacy rate.
Prevalence of a very low income level.
Failure of people to satisfy their basic needs.
g12-civics.e: A high average life expectancy and a high literacy rate are key indicators of human development and high quality of life, which are opposite to the indicators of poverty.

g12-economics.t: Short-run equilibrium of the monopolist is a point where
g12-economics.e: A monopolist, like any rational profit-maximizing firm, achieves short-run equilibrium at the output level where total profits are maximized (where MR = MC).

g12-economics.t:
If the Real GDP of country "A" in the year 2023 is 19,550,000 dollar and in the year 2022 it was 18,600,000
dollar, then the real GDP growth in 2023 as compared to the previous year will be equal to
g12-economics.e: The real GDP growth rate is calculated as [(Real GDP in 2023 - Real GDP in 2022) / Real GDP in 2022] * 100 = [(19,550,000 - 18,600,000) / 18,600,000] * 100 = 5.11%.

g12-economics.t:
What was the goal of sustainable development and poverty reduction program (SDPRP) assigned by Ethiopian
Peoples’ Revolutionary Democratic Front?
o: A massive push to accelerate economic growth
Unleashing the potentials of Ethiopia's women
Capacity building in the public and private sector
g12-economics.e: The Sustainable Development and Poverty Reduction Programme ran from 2002/03 to 2004/05 and was built on five goals: Agricultural Development Led Industrialisation, food security, decentralisation and empowerment, capacity building in the public and private sector, and reform of the justice system and civil service. Capacity building in the public and private sector is on that list, so it is the answer. The other three options are strategic goals of the next plan, PASDEP, which covered 2005/06 to 2009/10.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following terms explains an economy characterized by low carbon usage, resource efficiency
and socially inclusive?
g12-economics.e: According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), a green economy is defined as one that is low carbon, resource efficient, and socially inclusive.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following is a measure of inequality which is often expressed by the ratio of the area between
the Lorenz curve and a 45 0 line and the total area under the 45 0 line?
g12-economics.e: The Gini Coefficient is a standard measure of inequality, calculated as the ratio of the area between the Lorenz curve and the 45-degree line of perfect equality to the total area under the 45-degree line.

g12-economics.t: Compared to other African countries, Ethiopia is more successful in terms of
g12-economics.e: Ethiopia's clearest transport success is air transport and civil aviation. Ethiopian Airlines flies to more destinations than any other African carrier, runs a large cargo business and has made Addis Ababa the main air hub of the continent. Road density is still low by African standards, the railway network is short and new, and the light rail is a single city service, so none of the other three can be described as a lead over other African countries. (1)

g12-economics.t: Which one of the following is separately categorized under the Sustainable Development Goals?
o: Combat HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases
g12-economics.e: Responsible consumption and production is SDG Goal 12, whereas reducing child mortality, combating major diseases, and achieving universal primary education were distinct goals under the predecessor MDG framework.

g12-economics.t:
In a hypothetical country, (K) the number of employed labor is 25 million and the number of unemployed labors
is 5 million. Moreover, the total adult population of the country is given as 80 million. How much is the labor
force participation rate?
g12-economics.e: The labor force consists of both the employed and unemployed (25 + 5 = 30 million). The labor force participation rate is (Labor Force / Adult Population) * 100 = (30 million / 80 million) * 100 = 37.5%

g12-economics.t:
Suppose an Ethiopian importer is importing commodities by taking a full advantage of the deductions or
incentives approved in the tax schedule by the government to reduce its tax obligation. Which one of the
following terms reflects such kind of a tax non-compliance problem?
g12-economics.e: Tax avoidance involves utilizing legal methods, such as approved deductions and government tax incentives, to minimize the amount of tax owed.

g12-economics.t: In macroeconomics, the current consumption expenditure is likely to increase due to
o: expectation of lower price in the future
g12-economics.e: An expectation of higher future income shifts current consumption upwards as households feel wealthier and increase their current spending in anticipation of their future gains.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following is correct about the key strategic pillars of the ten-year development plan after
reform?
o: Building regional monopoly power and economy
Quality economic growth and shared prosperity
g12-economics.e: The ten year development plan for 2021 to 2030 lists ten strategic pillars, and the first one is quality economic growth and shared prosperity. The other pillars include productivity and competitiveness, private sector led growth, a resilient green economy and gender and social inclusion. Choice D is the trap: the real pillar is gender and social inclusion, and the option prints exclusion, which is the problem the plan sets out to remove. Choice C also reverses a pillar, since the plan calls for private sector led growth.

g12-economics.t:
When an insurance company provides fringe benefits on the basis of an average rate over a set of employees
and guarantees them to participate in the program, then this can be seen as a solution for which one of the
following problem?
g12-economics.e: Adverse selection occurs when high-risk individuals are more likely to buy insurance. Group coverage with mandatory participation solves this by averaging risk across all employees, preventing low-risk individuals from opting out.

g12-economics.t: Which type of tax is imposed and payable on luxury items according to the Ethiopian tax policy?
g12-economics.e: Excise taxes are selective taxes levied on specific luxury items, such as expensive cars and perfumes, as well as socially harmful products like tobacco and alcohol. (1)

g12-economics.t:
The unemployment rate for an economy is 4%. The labor force is estimated to be 55 million. What is the number
of unemployed people in millions?
g12-economics.e: The unemployment rate is the number of unemployed people divided by the labour force, times 100. Rearranged, the number of unemployed equals the rate times the labour force. Write the rate as a decimal: 4 percent is 0.04. Unemployed = 0.04 × 55 million = 2.2 million A quick check: 4 percent is a small share, so the answer must be far smaller than the 55 million labour force. That rules out choices B, C and D at once.

g12-economics.t: What is the role of the National Bank of Ethiopia?
o: Provision of loans to the individual farmers
g12-economics.e: The National Bank of Ethiopia is the country's central bank. It issues currency, holds foreign reserves, sets monetary policy and licenses and supervises banks, insurers and microfinance institutions, which is the regulation of the financial sector. Lending to individual farmers is the work of commercial banks and microfinance institutions, and collecting taxes is the job of the revenue authority, so A, B and C belong to other bodies.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following is the key priority area that is considered to be the basis for the locally developed
economic reform program recently?
g12-economics.e: Inclusive financial sector development is a key priority under the macroeconomic pillar of Ethiopia's Home-Grown Economic Reform (HGER) program, aiming to expand access to finance and savings mobilization.

g12-economics.t:
In Ethiopia, which of the following has got particular attention in the past yet characterized as the lowest
productive in its performance?
g12-economics.e: The agricultural sector has historically received substantial policy focus in Ethiopia (such as through the ADLI strategy), yet it remains characterized by very low productivity due to traditional farming practices and reliance on rainfed systems.

g12-economics.t: One of the following is considered to be fiscal policy tool. Which one is it?
g12-economics.e: Taxation is a primary tool of fiscal policy, alongside government spending, used by the government to manage economic activity and aggregate demand. (1)

g12-economics.t:
A firm produces 10 units of output at a total cost of 500 birr. When output increases to 11 units, total cost rises
to 540 birr. The marginal cost of the 11th unit is:
g12-economics.e: Marginal cost (MC) = change in total cost / change in quantity = (540 - 500) / (11 - 10) = 40 / 1 = 40 birr. MC is the additional cost of producing one more unit. (1)

g12-economics.t: Which theory provides a more realistic explanation of consumer choice?
g12-economics.e: Ordinal utility theory is considered more realistic because it only requires consumers to rank preferences (prefer A over B) rather than assign numerical utility values. This avoids the unrealistic assumption that utility is measurable cardinally. Indifference curve analysis is based on ordinal utility.

g12-economics.t: Among the followings, which one is the objective of the Home Grown Economic Reform?
o: Transition from private to public sector-led growth
g12-economics.e: The Home Grown Economic Reform was launched with three central objectives: sustaining rapid growth, keeping a stable macroeconomic environment by reducing debt vulnerabilities, and creating enough lasting jobs. Maintaining macroeconomic stability is therefore an objective. Choices A and B state harmful outcomes, and choice C runs the reform backwards, because it aims to move gradually from public to private sector led growth.

g12-economics.t: If the economy is facing deficient demand, which one of the following fiscal policy should be applied?
g12-economics.e: To combat deficient aggregate demand (recession), expansionary fiscal policy should be implemented, which involves increasing government expenditure or decreasing taxes.

g12-economics.t: The greatest contribution to Ethiopia's agricultural GDP comes from the
g12-economics.e: Ethiopian agriculture is made up of crop production, livestock, and forestry with fishery. The largest share of agricultural GDP comes from the crop production sub sector, where smallholder farmers grow cereals, pulses, oilseeds and cash crops such as coffee. Livestock is second and matters a lot for exports and household income, but it is still smaller than crops. Forestry and fishery contribute the least, and pastoral farming is a farming system, not a sub sector.

g12-economics.t: Which one of the following indicates the direct health dimension of the impacts of climate change?
g12-economics.e: Malaria represents a direct health dimension of climate change, as rising temperatures and changing rainfall patterns expand the geographic range and transmission seasons of vector-borne diseases.

g12-economics.t: Which of the following institutions plays a major role in implementing fiscal decentralization in Ethiopia?
g12-economics.e: Fiscal decentralization in Ethiopia transfers revenue-raising and expenditure responsibilities to regional and woreda (district) governments. Regional state governments collect regional taxes, receive federal block grants, and manage local public services (education, health, agriculture) under the constitution.

g12-economics.t: In Ethiopia, which one of the following institution is responsible to collect tax on behalf of the government?
g12-economics.e: The Ministry of Revenues is the federal institution in Ethiopia officially mandated to administer and collect federal taxes and custom duties.

g12-economics.t:
Gemechu owns a sole proprietorship type of business and incurred a loss. Which one of the following could
result in the sale of his private house if his business assets are not enough to cover the business liabilities?
o: Not suitable for large scale operations
g12-economics.e: In a sole proprietorship, the owner has unlimited liability, meaning their personal assets (such as a private home) can be seized and sold to settle any unpaid debts of the business.

g12-economics.t: Among the following, which one is a macroeconomic issue?
o: Actions of an individual agent within an economy
Resource allocation or price determination as central problem
The economic activities of a consumer, a producer or industry
Structure and performance of the economy as a whole
g12-economics.e: While microeconomics deals with individual economic units (consumers, firms, and industries), macroeconomics focuses on aggregates and the structure and performance of the economy as a whole.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following principles of taxation states that the tax system should be able to yield enough
revenue so that it should not be forced to resort to deficit financing?
g12-economics.e: The principle of fiscal adequacy states that the government's tax revenue should be sufficient to cover its necessary public expenditures so that it does not need to rely heavily on deficit financing.

g12-economics.t: A tight monetary policy is applied in circumstances where there is
g12-economics.e: A tight (contractionary) monetary policy is implemented by the central bank to decrease the money supply and raise interest rates, aiming to reduce aggregate demand and curb high inflation.

g12-economics.t: Which one of the following is the major role of non-banking financial institutions?
o: Serving as intermediary between borrowers and lenders
g12-economics.e: Non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) complement commercial banks by facilitating bank-related financial services such as investment, risk pooling, and contractual savings.

g12-economics.t: Which one of the following is among the key strategic pillars of the ten-year development plan in the homegrown economic reform period?
o: Quality economic growth and shared prosperity
A massive push to accelerate economic growth
g12-economics.e: The Ten-Year Development Plan (2021-2030) of Ethiopia, formulated during the homegrown economic reform period, identifies 'Quality economic growth and shared prosperity' as its first strategic pillar.

g12-economics.t:
Which one of the following is duly emphasized in one of the home-grown economic reform called sectoral
reform?
g12-economics.e: The sectoral reform pillar of the HGER targets five key sectors to drive economic growth: Agriculture, Manufacturing, Mining, ICT, and Tourism.

g12-english.t:
II. Language Focus (Questions 33–65)
In summer, she usually moves away ______ her family to attend a special camp.
g12-english.e: The preposition "from" is used with "move away" to indicate the person or place being left. "Move away from" means to leave a place or person behind. "In summer, she usually moves away from her family..." (1)

g12-english.t: the take Bikila first to Abebe gold ever an was Olympic home African
o: Abebe Bikila was ever the first African gold to take home an Olympic medal.
The first African Abebe Bikila was ever to take home an Olympic gold medal.
Abebe Bikila was the first African to ever take home an Olympic gold medal.
Abebe Bikila ever take an Olympic gold medal to home was the first African.
g12-english.e: Option D represents the standard grammatical structure for this historical fact: 'Abebe Bikila was the first African to ever take home an Olympic gold medal.'

g12-english.t: Lilu: Do you speak Italian? You:_____________.
g12-english.e: 'Just a little' is a standard short response indicating limited proficiency when asked 'Do you speak Italian?'.

g12-english.t: in/ can/ her/ and/ talk/ bring/ we.
o: We and her talk can bring in
We can talk her and bring in
Bring her in and we can talk
We bring her in and can talk
g12-english.e: Option D successfully links an imperative clause and a coordinate clause ('Bring her in and we can talk') using all of the given words correctly.

g12-english.t: Our agricultural products are mostly ______ to Europe and the Middle East.
g12-english.e: Goods or agricultural products sold and sent to other countries or regions (like Europe and the Middle East) are 'exported'.

g12-english.t: The professor __________ I met is from Kenya.
g12-english.e: The relative pronoun 'whom' is used because the professor is the object of the verb 'met' in the relative clause.

g12-english.t:
The main factor that led to the disbanding of the union is unfair distribution of income among members. Some of 
the leaders were absurdly egocenteric:
g12-english.e: The word 'main' is synonymous with 'principal,' which means first in order of importance or chief.

g12-english.t:
During the last century vaccination programs were introduced in most countries around the world. Before this,
thousands f people, especially children, used to die of infectious diseases every year. This is most likely taken
from the ______________ section of an essay.
g12-english.e: Providing historical context and general background information about a topic is characteristic of the introduction of an essay.

g12-english.t: My father is not ________old______ yours; he is only 53 years old.
g12-english.e: The comparison of equality in the negative is formed using 'not as + adjective + as', making 'as...as' the correct choice. (1)

g12-english.t:
Daba: Students at university should be totally free to choose their field of study so that they can be successful.
Adugna: ________but we should also consider the needs of society so that we have skilled human power in
every field.
g12-english.e: Adugna starts with a concession and uses 'but' to introduce a counterargument. 'That's a good point' acknowledges Daba's opinion before offering this contrasting perspective. (1)

g12-english.t: Which one of the following is taken form an informal letter?
o: wish me good luck for my math exam.
I would like to apply for the positon of assistant secretary.
I am writing to complain about the following damages.
I enclose my curriculum vitae for your attention.
g12-english.e: 'Wish me good luck for my math exam' uses an informal, conversational tone appropriate for a personal letter to a friend or family member.

g12-english.t: I wish I were not your teacher.
o: my sister was to be your teacher.
A. I am unhappy that I were not your teacher
B. I am very happy that I am not your teacher
g12-english.e: The subjunctive "I wish I were not..." expresses a regret about the present reality, meaning the actual fact is "I am your teacher" (written with a minor typographical error as "A am your teacher").

g12-english.t:
I will never forget my stay in this company. I enjoyed working with you as my boss and I ____________ meeting
you again sometime in my life.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'look forward to' is grammatically followed by a gerund noun phrase, which fits perfectly with 'meeting you again'. (1)

g12-english.t: I was__________when I heard the news of her mother's death.
g12-english.e: 'Shocked' expresses the profound grief and sudden distress typically caused by tragic news such as a death.

g12-english.t: He seems to be __________ cooking but I am quite the opposite. I rather enjoy eating.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'fond of' means liking something. The speaker contrasts the other person's love of cooking with their own love of eating instead.

g12-english.t: As used in paragraph 1, which word from those given below is similar in meaning to 'gorge' ?
g12-english.e: The verb "gorge" means to eat greedily or to fill oneself to capacity, which is synonymous with "stuff" in this context.

g12-english.t: My holiday was never_______________. I could use every minute for something enjoyable.
g12-english.e: 'Boring' provides the exact antonymous contrast to spending 'every minute for something enjoyable'.

g12-english.t: I would like _________________ her before she leaves. There is a big secret she didn't want to tell the family.
g12-english.e: The expression 'would like' is followed by a 'to'-infinitive, making 'to see' the correct grammatical choice.

g12-english.t: You: I know your favourite pastime. Your friend:_________________
g12-english.e: The statement 'I know...' is naturally challenged or replied to with the auxiliary verb 'do': 'No, you don't.' (1)

g12-english.t:
They kept trying hard to bring him to the position of chairmanship. Unfortunately, however, members chose
someone else so much unexpected.
g12-english.e: In this context, 'trying hard' is best represented by 'struggling', which means making strenuous or great efforts to achieve a difficult goal.

g12-english.t:
Everybody understands that most of you worked very hard _______ you would pass this test. But you don't have 
to lose hope if the result happens to be against your expectation.
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'so that' is used to introduce a clause of purpose, explaining why they worked very hard (with the goal of passing the test).

g12-english.t:
If the Ethiopian government collected taxes with a great effort, the country’s ______ would rise by a higher
percentage.
g12-english.e: The income generated by a government, especially through taxes, is formally referred to as 'revenue'.

g12-english.t: Mustefa: Excuse me, can you tell me where the Registrar's office is? Hallima: ________ I am stranger here
o: Why do you want to go there?
g12-english.e: Because Hallima is a stranger and cannot provide directions, 'I'm sorry I don't know' is the most polite and appropriate response.

g12-english.t: Kebede: Do you think their plan is going to work out? Nigist: _____________________
o: Who knows? Let's wait and see.
By the way, who has masterminded it?
g12-english.e: The question asks for a prediction on whether a plan will succeed, and 'Who knows? Let's wait and see' is a common idiomatic expression used when the future outcome is uncertain.

g12-english.t:
Out in the office behind his house, Lemma is sweating over his newspaper column. His feet are propped up on
his desk, and his computer keyboard sits on his lap. This is most likely taken from a piece of writing that is
g12-english.e: The passage uses visual and sensory details ('sweating', 'feet are propped up', 'sits on his lap') to paint a vivid picture of a scene, which is typical of descriptive writing.

g12-english.t: Us him and go up and pick
o: Let him go and pick up us.
Let him up and go pick us.
Let him go up and us pick.
Let us go and pick him up
g12-english.e: 'Let us go and pick him up' is the only grammatically correct rearrangement. In phrasal verbs with a pronoun object, the pronoun must go between the verb and the particle ('pick him up', not 'pick up him/us').

g12-english.t: You smoke a lot; you should stop _____ and you will feel much healthier.
g12-english.e: Stop + the -ing form means end the activity, which is what a heavy smoker should do. Stop + to + verb would mean pause in order to do something else. Option B, smoked, cannot follow stop at all, because stop takes either -ing or to + verb.

g12-english.t:
Reservationist: Can I have the dates for your departure and return? Customer: Yes, I want to leave on July 27
and return on 30. Reservationist: ______________________ Did you say you wanted to return on July 30.
Customer: Sorry. I didn't make myself clear. I want to return on August 30.
o: I'm sorry; I didn't follow what you said.
Do you have a flight phobia?
That is your first time to book a ticket.
g12-english.e: The reservationist's request for clarification ('Did you say you wanted to return on July 30') naturally follows the polite statement 'I'm sorry; I didn't follow what you said.'

g12-english.t:
I would have married her ________________ I had known her dad was one of the wealthiest in the town. I was
just unlucky.
g12-english.e: In this third conditional sentence, 'if only' acts as an emphatic conditional conjunction meaning 'if indeed' or 'I wish', expressing regret about not knowing the father's wealth.

g12-english.t: Where would you write a request for an action in the format of a formal letter?
o: in the Body of the letter
g12-english.e: Any request for action or detailed communication in a formal letter belongs in the body of the letter, typically in the concluding paragraph of the body.

g12-english.t: My classmate goes to school by bus_______ I walk every day.
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'whereas' is used to contrast two facts directly in a single sentence.

g12-english.t:
same passage
What concerns are there about the long-term environmental impact of GMOs?
o: GMOs have no effect on the environment.
g12-english.e: The last paragraph names two long-term worries about GMOs: the environmental impact and 'the potential loss of biodiversity'. Option B states that loss. Option C says GMOs improve biodiversity, which is the opposite of what the passage raises as a concern. (1)

g12-english.t: If you send a plagiarist to jail for one-year service, the most likely, what is the consequence of the decision?
g12-english.e: Sending a person to jail is a criminal penalty, which represents a legal consequence of plagiarism.

g12-english.t: The whole building collapsed when it was hit by a missile. Only two __________ children were found alive in.
g12-english.e: In this context, 'fortunate' (meaning lucky or favored by fortune) is the most appropriate adjective to describe the children who luckily survived the building collapse.

g12-english.t: Mother:_______________? You: I put in just a little.
o: when did you put in salt
why did you put in salt
how much salt did you put in
g12-english.e: The answer 'just a little' specifies a quantity of an uncountable noun (salt), which answers the question 'How much salt did you put in?'.

g12-english.t: I don't have a long standing acquaintance with Lojo, but I already feel that I _______ her for years.
g12-english.e: 'Know' is a stative verb and cannot be used in continuous tenses. The present perfect 'have known' represents a state that started in the past and continues to the present.

g12-english.t:
When the police arrived, the burglars _______ away with the money. But there is hope that they would be
caught.
g12-english.e: The past perfect tense 'had already made' is used to show that the burglars' escape occurred before the police arrived in the past.

g12-english.t: Let me withdraw some money from ATM______ we come across something interesting in the super market.
g12-english.e: 'In case' is used to talk about doing something as a precaution against a possible future situation.

g12-english.t: Tadesse: Why is the roof leaking? Carpenter: _______________ it hasn't been serviced for long.
o: The reason as a fact is that
This is due to the fact that
Yes, it is because of the reason that
g12-english.e: 'This is due to the fact that' is a correct and formal prepositional phrase used to introduce a clause explaining a cause.

g12-english.t: My grade this semester is _______ than my first semester's.
g12-english.e: When comparing two things (this semester's grade and the first semester's), the comparative form 'better' is used. 'Much' acts as an intensifier, making 'much better' the correct choice.

g12-english.t: Doctor: _____ Bonsa: About four days now.
o: How often do you see these symptoms?
Have you seen these symptoms for about four days?
How long have you had these symptoms?
g12-english.e: "About four days now" gives a length of time, so the question has to ask about length. The present perfect in "How long have you had these symptoms?" fits something that started in the past and is still going on. B is tempting because it also asks about time, but "how often" would be answered with something like "twice a day".

g12-english.t:
Brother: life is getting more and more expensive here. Shall we leave for another place?
Sister:____________________.
o: I guess it is the same everywhere.
How much do you need for your food?
how much do you earn now?
True! Everybody is complaining these days.
g12-english.e: The brother asks a question: shall we leave for another place? The reply has to answer that proposal, and "I guess it is the same everywhere" answers it with a reason for staying. D is tempting because it agrees that prices are high, but agreeing about the cost says nothing about moving, which is what was asked.

g12-english.t: in you girl about slim, are pretty the talking neighborhood tall, this?
o: Are you this pretty, tall, slim girl talking about in the neighborhood?
Are you talking about this tall, slim, pretty girl in the neighborhood?
You are about the pretty, talking, tall girl in this slim neighborhood?
This pretty, tall, girl in the neighborhood talking about you are slim?
g12-english.e: This option is the only one that uses all the words from the stem to form a grammatically correct, natural question in English: "Are you talking about this tall, slim, pretty girl in the neighborhood?" (1)

g12-english.t: Cub is to a Lion: __________ is to a Cow.
g12-english.e: This is an analogy question comparing animals to their offspring: a cub is the offspring of a lion, and a calf is the offspring of a cow.

g12-english.t: New situations always made me nervous. Which sentences is like to come next?
o: I stood timidly by the side of the changing room.
I changed into my bathing suit.
my first swimming lesson was no exception.
after a couple of minutes the teacher came over.
g12-english.e: Option B provides a smooth transition from the general opening claim ('New situations always made me nervous') to a specific illustrative experience ('my first swimming lesson was no exception').

g12-english.t: Sosina: Do you like that funky hairstyle? Hirut: _______________
o: Gosh! It is so weird to me.
I see so many girls wearing it.
Mom always makes fun of such a style.
It is all over now! What fashion is that?
g12-english.e: Sosina asks for Hirut's personal opinion about a hairstyle. Option C directly answers with Hirut's reaction ("Gosh! It is so weird to me"), indicating a dislike for it.

g12-english.t: Which of the following words can be synonymous with the word ' dedicated ' in paragraph 3, line 4?
g12-english.e: To be 'dedicated' to a task or goal means to be deeply 'committed' and devoted to it.

g12-english.t: "Just a moment, please!" "The room _______," said the teacher.
g12-english.e: The exclamation 'Just a moment, please!' indicates that the action is currently in progress, requiring the present continuous passive form 'is being cleaned'.

g12-english.t: My friend is sometimes hard to convince, but I like him ___.
g12-english.e: 'Nonetheless' is an adverb meaning 'in spite of that' or 'nevertheless', which correctly contrasts liking the friend despite him being hard to convince.

g12-english.t: Which of the following is similar in meaning to " glossy " as used in paragraph 2?
g12-english.e: "Glossy" refers to a shiny, smooth surface, making "smooth" the closest synonym in the context of paper types.

g12-english.t: It was all tiring, but we had no other option. I really hate such ___________________tasks.
g12-english.e: The word 'exhausting' is synonymous with 'extremely tiring', perfectly matching the context of performing very tiring tasks.

g12-english.t:
Thanks to technology, we ________ carry a lot of cash with us when we go shopping. We can use mobile
banking to make payments.
g12-english.e: 'Don't have to' is used to express an absence of necessity or obligation. Since mobile banking is available, carrying cash is no longer necessary.

g12-english.t: Belay: My house has been broken into. I am thinking of hiring security. Amare:____________________________.
o: Why do they do such a nasty thing?
You may also report to the police.
In fact, that happens to a number of people.
g12-english.e: Recommending that the victim also notify law enforcement ('You may also report to the police') is the most constructive and appropriate conversational response.

g12-english.t: You: What does our new English teacher look like? Friend: ___________
g12-english.e: The question 'What does he look like?' asks for a physical description, which is perfectly answered by 'He's short, but well-built.'

g12-english.t:
I am giving up the idea of starting an MA programme at Jombola University. Admission with them is in August,
but I ____________ from here by then. I will still have one more course to do.
g12-english.e: The future perfect tense ('won't have graduated') is required here because of the time reference 'by then' (by August).

g12-english.t: Due to economic and cultural factors, many children in the countryside __________ of school.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'drop out' means to abandon a course of study before finishing it, which fits the context of leaving school due to economic and cultural factors.

g12-english.t: I have no doubt he would win the scholarship. He is the_______________ of all.
g12-english.e: When comparing one individual against all members of a group ('of all'), the superlative degree 'the most talented' is required. (1)

g12-english.t: He was doing the washing up _______ she was cleaning the house. We like that they help one another.
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'while' is used to connect two continuous actions occurring at the same time in the past.

g12-english.t: Kidist: _______________ Hana: With sugar, please.
o: Is it good to drink coffee without sugar
Do you like your coffee with sugar
How much sugar do you like in your coffee
Would you prefer your coffee with or without sugar
g12-english.e: The question 'Would you prefer your coffee with or without sugar?' is an alternative question that is naturally resolved with the response 'With sugar, please.'

g12-english.t: Kuku: Are you she is arriving this weekend? Eleni: ____________________
o: No doubt! She has her seat confirmed.
The weekend is going to be rainy.
They have prepared a lot of things to welcome her.
I think she is taking a plane to change at Dubai.
g12-english.e: Kuku asks for confirmation of certainty ("Are you [sure] she is arriving this weekend?"), and "No doubt! She has her seat confirmed" directly expresses full certainty.

g12-english.t:
Driver: My Toyota car is still perfect after 10 years on the road.
Mechanic: _____________________________________
g12-english.e: As a professional, the mechanic's generalization that 'Toyota cars are the best' directly validates the driver's experience of their car being perfect after ten years.

g12-english.t:
I have _______ things to do before I leave for the meeting. So, I have to lock myself in and work with no
interruption.
g12-english.e: 'A lot of' is used with plural countable nouns like 'things' to show a large quantity, which justifies the need to work with no interruption.

g12-english.t:
Student 1: I'm sorry. I don't remember. Have you seen them?
Student 2: ___________________________
o: What were they doing? They must be our friends.
I was busy doing my homework.
Probably, It was an empty room.
Sure. I've seen them with my naked eyes.
g12-english.e: Student 2's response 'Sure. I've seen them with my naked eyes' directly and emphatically answers Student 1's question 'Have you seen them?'. (1)

g12-english.t:
It is sad that COVID-19 has already caused a lot of damage to many countries of the world. _______ due to the
vaccines administered all over the world, there are signs that the rate of infection is declining.
g12-english.e: 'However' is used at the start of a sentence to introduce a contrasting idea, separated by a comma or introducing a contrasting adverbial phrase.

g12-english.t: ___________________ Would i say about this exam later at home.
g12-english.e: Negative inversion occurs when a negative phrase like 'Not a word' begins the sentence, inverting the subject and auxiliary verb ('would I say').

g12-english.t: My grandfather's face was ______________ with age.
g12-english.e: With advancing age, a person's skin loses elasticity and becomes 'wrinkled.'

g12-english.t: Belay: everybody should contribute. This is for the good of the community. Kiros: ________________.
o: Each of us is to pay birr 5,000
g12-english.e: "I can't agree more" means complete agreement, which is the natural reply to somebody calling for a contribution for the good of the community. D is tempting because it also sounds like taking part, but naming a figure of 5,000 birr answers a question about the amount that nobody has asked. (1)

g12-english.t: Student: Sir, We've won the inter-school competition. Our school stood first. Director: _____________________
o: What great news! I'm pleased to hear that.
Really? I actually knew two of the judges.
This is our first time to participate.
Wasn't the competition stiff as such?
g12-english.e: As the director of the school, expressing delight and congratulating the students with 'What great news! I'm pleased to hear that' is the most appropriate and supportive reaction to winning a competition.

g12-english.t:
We cannot be talking about failure of plans every year. What have you done about them and where and when did 
you succeed?
g12-english.e: A 'miscarriage' of a plan refers to its failure or lack of success, making it the closest synonym to 'failure' in this context.

g12-english.t:
You: Guess what! I bought a car.
Friend: _____________________
o: Where are cars sold in this city?
Are you serious? You must be joking!
I also want to buy a new one.
g12-english.e: Buying a car is a major accomplishment, and expressing surprise with 'Are you serious? You must be joking!' is a typical, friendly response.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following could be an opening to your informal letter?
o: I am writing this to complain…
this is in response to your…
I have received your letter of 28 May.
g12-english.e: 'How are you darling?' is highly affectionate and informal, making it perfect for opening an informal letter, while the other options are typical of business or formal correspondence.

g12-english.t: It to wanted you today me do.
o: you wanted me to do it today.
it wanted me today you to do.
today you wanted it me to do.
me wanted you to do it today.
g12-english.e: The standard English word order for this sentence is subject ('you'), verb ('wanted'), object pronoun ('me'), to-infinitive clause ('to do it'), and adverb of time ('today'): 'You wanted me to do it today.'

g12-english.t:
In Paragraph 3, the author says, "With the latter, it seems everyone loses out in one way or ..." What does "with
the latter" show?
g12-english.e: "The latter" refers to the second of two options; since the author notes that with the latter "everyone loses out," it must refer to a negative action like "creating disadvantages for others." (1)

g12-english.t: Tutu: I am leaving for US on Monday. US, California. Titi: ________ Could you repeat that, please?
o: That is too good to be true
Are you trying to fool me?
g12-english.e: 'Sorry, I didn't catch that' is a polite expression used when you did not hear or understand what someone said, prompting them to repeat it. (1)

g12-english.t:
At least half of the first year students surveyed reported adopting writing strategies that involved the use of
their first language. This could be a typical example of a research report based on a research topic entitled:
o: First Year students' First Language in Writing
First Year students' First Language Use.
First Year students' Strategies of Using First Language
g12-english.e: The finding reports a specific strategy (using the first language) identified among students, fitting under an overarching investigation of 'First Year Students' Writing Strategies.'

g12-english.t: ______________you and your wife have concocted this. I have never said that.
g12-english.e: The correlative conjunction 'both' correctly pairs with 'and' when referring to two subjects ('you and your wife').

g12-english.t: Stranger: excuse me, _______________ You: I'm a stranger her myself
o: tell me where is the post office?
Do you tell me where the post office is?
you tell where post office is
Can you tell me where the post office is?
g12-english.e: 'Can you tell me where the post office is?' is a standard polite indirect question asking for directions, which elicits the common response 'I'm a stranger here myself'.

g12-english.t: Choose the correctly spelt word.
g12-english.e: 'Expenditure' is correctly spelled. The others are misspelled versions of 'particularly', 'traditional', and 'photograph'.

g12-english.t: Mother:______________? Daughter: well, I placed the egg carefully in the jar.
o: when did you place the egg in the jar
who placed the egg in the jar
did you place the egg in the jar
g12-english.e: The daughter describes an action in a sequence of events, which best answers 'What did you do next?'.

g12-english.t: Mine is from Germany, __________ hers is from China. Can't you see the difference then?
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'whereas' is used to contrast two facts directly in a single sentence. (1)

g12-english.t:
Interviewer: You said that you left your previous work place because the organization was old-fashioned. What
do you mean? Candidate: _______. The management is not open to change; they always want to do things the
old way.
o: Let me repeat what I just said
Let me say it again loudly
Let me re-phrase what I just said
I will say that again if you want
g12-english.e: When an interviewer asks 'What do you mean?', they are asking for clarification, so the candidate naturally introduces their explanation with 'Let me re-phrase what I just said'.

g12-english.t:
Each one of us______________________ help those affected by the drought. It is immoral to leave them to
starve.
g12-english.e: 'Ought to' is the modal verb specifically used to express moral obligation and duty, which directly corresponds to the context given: 'It is immoral to leave them to starve.'

g12-english.t: Shito: we're going to Lalibela for a tour Next week. Isn't that marvellous? Aster:
o: It might take a few days to get there.
When are you planning to come back?
Brilliant. You may also consider seeing BahirDar.
Why do people spend money going around?
g12-english.e: 'Brilliant. You may also consider seeing BahirDar' directly agrees with the excitement ('Isn't that marvellous?') and offers a helpful travel suggestion.

g12-english.t: the elsewhere is of unfriendly town people full from.
o: The town is unfriendly full of people from elsewhere.
The town is full of unfriendly people from elsewhere.
Unfriendly people from elsewhere is full of the town.
From elsewhere is the town full of unfriendly people.
g12-english.e: Reassembling the words in Option D gives 'The town is full of unfriendly people from elsewhere', which is a grammatically perfect and natural English sentence. (1)

g12-english.t: The price of goods are known for their variability because they increase and decrease every other day.
g12-english.e: Prices that increase and decrease constantly are characterized by 'variability,' which is synonymous with 'fluctuation.'

g12-english.t: Roberto was__________from his job for being caught red handed stealing confidential document.
g12-english.e: To be "sacked" means to be dismissed or fired from a job, which is the appropriate consequence for being caught stealing confidential documents.

g12-english.t: Peter has reorganized his files ______ he can easily find what he is looking for.
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'so that' is used to introduce a clause of purpose, explaining why Peter reorganized his files.

g12-english.t: School buses should always be driven by a/an _______ driver.
g12-english.e: For safety and legal reasons, school buses must always be driven by a 'licensed' driver.

g12-english.t: I don't understand why he suspected us. ____________________ From among us would want his money.
g12-english.e: 'No one' provides the negative subject needed to explain why the suspicion was baseless ('No one from among us would want his money').

g12-english.t:
Chaltu is very considerate but she could not tolerate people who do not have a sense of ______. That’s why she
always cracks jokes and makes her audiences laugh.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'cracks jokes and makes her audiences laugh' directly indicates that she values and possesses a 'sense of humor'.

g12-english.t: Getahun: what was your hliday like? Fetiha: ________
o: it was nice but the weather was not good.
g12-english.e: The question 'What was it like?' asks for a description of the holiday; 'it was nice but the weather was not good' properly provides that description.

g12-english.t: For and join come us celebration the?
o: Come and join the celebration for us.
Come and join for us the celebration.
Come and join us for the celebration.
For us the celebration come and join.
g12-english.e: 'Come and join us for the celebration' is the standard imperative construction with the transitive verb 'join' taking the direct object 'us' followed by the prepositional phrase 'for the celebration'.

g12-english.t: If Sofia worked hard, she ________ good mark.
g12-english.e: This is a second conditional sentence ('If' + simple past + 'would' + base verb) used to describe a hypothetical situation. Thus, 'would get' is the correct verb form.

g12-english.t: If you go to a new place, your behavior and manner should harmonize with that of the people you meet there.
g12-english.e: To 'harmonize with' means to blend in well or fit with, which is closely synonymous with 'integrate'.

g12-english.t: His brothers are running ___________ money. Therefore, they need some.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'run out of' means to use up a supply of something so that none is left, which fits the context of needing money.

g12-english.t: A witness was able to____________my story that the accident was not my fault.
g12-english.e: 'Substantiate' means to provide evidence to prove the truth of a claim or story.

g12-english.t:
Manager: What happened to those new machines?
Technician: ____________________
o: Very frustrating! None of them is working.
May be, they are not good machines.
Shall we put them on auction?
Amazing! They are new and well-designed.
g12-english.e: The technician's role is to report the status of the machines to the manager. Saying 'Very frustrating! None of them is working' directly answers what happened to them.

g12-english.t: If we are not able to ______________ ideas accurately, misunderstandings would naturally crop up.
g12-english.e: 'Communicate' is the most suitable verb here because failing to transmit or share ideas accurately leads directly to misunderstandings.

g12-english.t: Aleltu:________________? Thomas: sorry. I am busy with my assignment.
o: Have you seen the report I compiled?
Could you help me organize the report?
Have you finished ding your assignment?
Would you read the report when you are ready?
g12-english.e: Thomas's response is an apology declining a request for help due to being busy, which logically follows a polite request like 'Could you help me organize the report?'.

g12-english.t: Way there similar co Way there similar cold apes in humans be no which to are.
o: There could be no way in which humans are similar to apes.
There are apes which could no way be in similar to humans.
There could be humans which no way are in similar to apes.
There are no humans which could be in way similar to apes.
g12-english.e: "There could be no way in which humans are similar to apes" is the only grammatically correct and meaningful arrangement of the scrambled words. (1)

g12-english.t: I wanted to buy the car, but it cost an arm and a leg. What should I do, Leliko? (cost an arm and a leg means)
g12-english.e: To cost an arm and a leg is to be very expensive, which explains why the speaker wanted the car but is asking what to do instead of buying it. Option C, a very low price, would leave the hesitation in the sentence unexplained.

g12-english.t: Driver: What's the matter? Policeman: You have violated a traffic rule._________________
o: How can we allow people like you?
When you see a red light, you should stop.
It is not my business. It is the minimum penalty.
I am sorry. The road is free. I failed to notice you.
g12-english.e: The policeman's role is to explain the violation; stating 'When you see a red light, you should stop' is a direct and logical follow-up to 'You have violated a traffic rule.' (1)

g12-english.t:
If you were to be a teacher, you ____________________have to join a college of education and take the
necessary training. You can't jump into the profession from the street.
g12-english.e: 'If you were to be...' is an unreal/hypothetical conditional (second conditional), which takes 'would' in the main clause ('you would have to...').

g12-english.t: We have known each other________childhood.
g12-english.e: 'Since' is used with the present perfect tense to indicate the starting point in time of an action or state (childhood).

g12-english.t:
It appears the combined effort exerted by the team significantly contributed to their success. In fact, we need to
take a lesson and reshape our strategy.
g12-english.e: 'Synergy' refers to the interaction or cooperation of two or more agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their individual effects.

g12-english.t: _______ she came home, I made her coffee. Then we sat together and had hours of talk and talk.
g12-english.e: 'When' is the correct temporal conjunction to show a sequence of events in the past (first she came home, then I made her coffee).

g12-english.t: Clean air ______ the well-being of people everywhere.
g12-english.e: 'Sustains' is the most appropriate verb here, meaning to strengthen, support, or keep something going over time.

g12-english.t:
"My coat was no the seat next to me. I took my passport out my pocket and put it in my bag in the luggage
rack." These lines are taken from a piece of writing that is most likely
g12-english.e: The excerpt recounts a chronological sequence of actions ('took my passport out', 'put it in my bag'), which is characteristic of narrative writing. (1)

g12-english.t: According to the passage, what does the word 'manure' in the fourth paragraph mean?
g12-english.e: The word 'manure' refers to organic matter, typically animal dung, used as an agricultural fertilizer to enrich the soil.

g12-english.t: The doctor told the nurse to have all the gadgets sterilized and make them ready for the operation this morning.
g12-english.e: In medical contexts, 'sterilized' means to be made free from bacteria or other microorganisms, which is synonymous with 'germ-free'.

g12-english.t: My mother was furious when she found out her friend hadn't told her the truth.
g12-english.e: 'Furious' means extremely angry or full of wild, fierce anger.

g12-english.t: People going to many invite party are to your you?
o: Are your many people going to invite you to party?
Are you going to invite many people to your party?
Are your many party going to you people to invite?
Are you going to many party to invite your people?
g12-english.e: 'Are you going to invite many people to your party?' correctly follows standard English question order: Auxiliary (Are) + Subject (you) + Verb phrase (going to invite) + Direct Object (many people) + Prepositional Phrase (to your party).

g12-english.t: I think she did an excellent job on her presentation.
g12-english.e: To agree with a positive statement starting with 'I think' (present simple), we use the auxiliary verb 'do' in the form 'So do I' (meaning 'I also think so').

g12-english.t:
Do you know __________ she had when she started the investment? In fact, she is so much business-minded
and now she has become a millionaire.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'how much' is used to ask or talk about uncountable quantities, such as money, which fits the context of investment and becoming a millionaire.

g12-english.t: Teacher: ________________. Student: I get out of bed.
o: What time do you get up?
What do you do first in the morning?
Who gets up first in your family?
Do you ever get up before six?
g12-english.e: The student's answer, "I get out of bed", names an action, not a time and not a person. The question that such an answer fits is "What do you do first in the morning?" A is the trap because it is about the same moment of the day, but a question with "what time" expects a clock time in the answer.

g12-english.t:
Boss: What was their argument in brief?
Subordinate: ________________________
o: They just kept talking. Nothing brief.
Yes, they always like to argue.
They want the group to leave now.
g12-english.e: The subordinate summarizes the core point of the argument ('They want the group to leave now') in response to the boss's request for a brief summary.

g12-english.t: After waiting for two hours, mom grew ________________ with my sister and decided to call her.
g12-english.e: Waiting for two hours makes a person 'impatient' (restless or irritated by delay). (1)

g12-english.t: pass / so that / working / the / can / hard / am / I / test.
o: I am hard working so that I can the test pass.
I am working hard so that I can pass the test.
I can pass the test so that I am working hard.
I can pass so that I am working hard the test.
g12-english.e: The correct sentence order is 'I am working hard so that I can pass the test,' where 'so that' introduces a purpose clause showing the reason for working hard.

g12-english.t: Did you know that Mary and Bedlu________________ married next week?
g12-english.e: 'Are going to get' is the standard way to express a planned future arrangement or event, such as a scheduled wedding next week.

g12-english.t:
The disagreement between the warring parties should be solved amicably. That seems to be the only way that
could lead to a win-win solution
g12-english.e: A 'disagreement' between opposing or warring parties is synonymous with a 'dispute.'

g12-english.t:
When you buy an item from a shop, you are usually given a one-year assurance so if it stops working, you can
get it fixed for free.
g12-english.e: An 'assurance' given by a seller to fix a product for free if it stops working within a specified period is called a 'guarantee'.

g12-english.t:
When we take an entrance examination like this, the results are almost always dual . So, we need to work hard
to be in the pass group and avoid failing.
g12-english.e: The context describes an exam with two possible outcomes (pass or fail); 'binary' means relating to or consisting of two components, which is synonymous with 'dual' here.

g12-english.t: Teacher: how far is the school from your home? Student: ___________________
g12-english.e: 'How far' asks for physical distance, making '3kms.' the correct answer.

g12-english.t:
II. Language Focus (Questions 33–65)
By the time the police arrived, the thief ______ away.
g12-english.e: This sentence uses the past perfect tense to show that one past action happened before another past action. "By the time the police arrived" (later past action), "the thief had run away" (earlier past action). The past perfect is formed with "had" + past participle.

g12-english.t: Muktar went to Jimma ______ see his old friends,
g12-english.e: The phrase 'in order to' is used to express purpose followed by a bare infinitive verb ('see').

g12-english.t:
They didn't want to pay us the money back. However, after many rounds of discussion, we __________ convince
them and now they have deposited it into our account.
g12-english.e: The past tense 'were able to' is used to express success in achieving something in a specific past situation, which fits the context of 'didn't want to pay us... but now they have deposited it.'

g12-english.t: Secretary: May I help you? Visitor: ________________.
o: Can I see the boss, please?
g12-english.e: "May I help you?" is an offer, and the natural reply states what you have come for. "Can I see the boss, please?" does that. B is the trap because it sounds polite, but it hands the question back to the secretary, who has already offered, so the conversation stops instead of moving on.

g12-english.t:
Dandir: is Addis Ababa getting more and more dangerous? People say there are gangs everywhere. Gemechu:
No, no. ________
o: this kind of behaviour simply won't be tolerated.
that's simply the best city can afford
g12-english.e: Gemechu disagrees with the claim about dangerous gangs by stating that 'it's simply an exaggeration.'

g12-english.t: According to a recent survey, young drivers are_______________ likely to have an accident.
g12-english.e: 'Likely' forms its superlative with 'most'; hence, 'the most likely' is the correct form to express the highest probability.

g12-english.t:
Why should the poor pay as much as the rich? First, the poor is already poor and nothing is to be drawn out of
poverty. Second, there is also a moral question of whether it would be just to add another burden to this group
already saddled with... This is taken a piece of writing that is most likely:
g12-english.e: The passage poses a rhetorical question and lays out numbered points ('First...', 'Second...') to persuade the reader of a moral viewpoint, which is characteristic of argumentative writing.

g12-english.t: You : How old are you? Lidet: __________________.
o: I'm the youngest in the family
g12-english.e: The question 'How old are you?' directly asks for the speaker's age, making 'Twenty-two' the correct and direct response.

g12-english.t: _____ you study diligently, you'll never understand trigonometry.
g12-english.e: "Unless" means "if not", and it works with the negative main clause: if you do not study diligently, you will never understand trigonometry. C is tempting because "if" fits the same slot in the sentence, but "If you study diligently, you'll never understand trigonometry" turns the advice upside down.

g12-english.t:
Everybody reacted in a strange way. It was a really ____________ blast that I could hear almost nothing of the
screams and yells around. It took me five minutes to realize what was going on.
g12-english.e: The word 'deafening' means extremely loud, which explains why the speaker 'could hear almost nothing' after the blast.

g12-english.t: There was a cheerful receptionist at the hotel; she always enjoyed amusing her guests.
g12-english.e: A 'cheerful' person is happy, optimistic, and welcoming, which is best matched by the synonym 'friendly' among the options.

g12-english.t: Teacher: I don't know why but I am feeling very dizzy. Friend: ________ see your doctor immediately. Right now!
g12-english.e: 'You had better' is used to give strong advice, especially in urgent situations, and is followed by the bare infinitive 'see'.

g12-english.t: The teacher told me ____________ to my friends during the exam.
g12-english.e: The negative reported imperative uses the structure 'not to + infinitive' (e.g., 'not to talk').

g12-english.t:
Whatever delicious food they make turns out to be ___________ to her. It seems she has some deep-seated
feeling towards the community.
g12-english.e: Because she holds a deep-seated negative prejudice against the community, even their 'delicious' food turns out to be 'disgusting' to her.

g12-english.t: I don't have a car, _______, I don't even have a driving license.
g12-english.e: The transition word 'Furthermore' is used to add extra, supporting information that reinforces the speaker's lack of a car. (1)

g12-english.t: Parents after of you which your take do?
o: After which did you take of your parents?
Which of your parents take after you did?
Did you take after which of your parents?
Which of your parents did you take after?
g12-english.e: 'Which of your parents did you take after?' is the only grammatically correct and natural rearrangement of the given words, using the phrasal verb 'take after' correctly.

g12-english.t:
Natural Calamity has become a challenge to most nations in developing countries. Mankind can no more ignore
the issue.
g12-english.e: A 'calamity' is an event causing great and often sudden damage or distress, which is synonymous with 'disaster'.

g12-english.t: At the meeting, the Chairman allowed ___ of opinions for
g12-english.e: The phrase 'diversity of opinions' refers to a range of different ideas and viewpoints, which fits perfectly in this context.

g12-english.t: It is a matter of time. ______ that good thing will come and when it comes, it will be a surprise.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'It is a matter of time' implies that the event will definitely happen eventually, making 'There is no doubt' the most logical continuation.

g12-english.t: The committee________ the issue thoroughly at the meeting yesterday.
g12-english.e: The time marker 'yesterday' indicates that the action is completed in the past, requiring the active past simple verb 'discussed'.

g12-english.t:
There are thousands of displaced people in different parts of the country who have no proper shelter, food or
cloth. Don't you think we ___________ help them?
g12-english.e: 'Ought to' is used to express moral obligation or duty, which fits the context of helping displaced people.

g12-english.t: Shop assistant: What can I help you? Customer: ___________________
o: Can you give me a jacket?
g12-english.e: 'I am just looking' is the standard polite response given by a customer in a store who does not require immediate assistance from a shop assistant.

g12-english.t: Passenger 1: the weather looks nice, doesn't it? Passenger 2: ___________________
o: would it be the same in Bahir Dar also?
it is like Bahir Dar, where we are going.
it is too hot this time of the year.
g12-english.e: Passenger 1 asks for confirmation with a tag question about the weather, and "yeah, but too unpredictable" provides a natural, conversational response.

g12-english.t:
Sisay: Have you ever heard that Natan and Dagmawit are getting married? Semegn: Oh, really? What a surprise.
_____
o: Of course, I heard about it
I'm very pleased to hear that
g12-english.e: Semegn says 'What a surprise', which is a warm reaction to news of a wedding, so the next line continues that pleasure: 'I'm very pleased to hear that', option A. Option B is the trap, because if he had already heard about it the news could not be a surprise. (1)

g12-english.t: I was send you the documents to review them as quickly as you can. They expect our comment early next week.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'go over' means to examine, check, or review something carefully.

g12-english.t:
Nearly ____________ of the invited guests appeared for the theatre and the manager was fuming about this. I
said nothing, but chose to keep silent.
g12-english.e: 'Nearly none' fits the context perfectly because the manager's anger ('fuming') indicates that almost no invited guests showed up.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following words is correctly spelt?
g12-english.e: "Restaurant" is the correct spelling, with the "au" in the middle and "ant" at the end. The other three are all misspelt: extension, cafeteria and volleyball. B is the trap because the ending sounds the same as in "attention", but the noun made from "extend" keeps the s of the verb, so it is extension.

g12-english.t: on have finished assignment your working project you?
o: Have you finished your assignment project on working?
Have you finished working on your project assignment?
Have you finished working your assignment on project?
Have you finished working on your assignment project?
g12-english.e: Put the scrambled words into the normal order of a yes or no question: auxiliary, subject, then the rest. That gives Have you finished working on your project assignment? B splits the phrasal verb and leaves on project stranded, and C attaches on working to the wrong noun. Note on this copy: option A uses the same words in a slightly different noun order and also reads correctly, so the item does not separate the two cleanly.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following is an appropriate ending to your letter of complaint to a company?
g12-english.e: A letter of complaint is a formal business communication, making the highly professional sign-off 'Sincerely,' the most appropriate option.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following is mentioned as a source of indoor pollutants?
g12-english.e: Cosmetics (such as sprays, perfumes, and powders) are widely recognized as a significant household source of indoor chemical pollutants.

g12-english.t:
The words below are NOT in the proper order. When put in the right order, they make a correct English sentence.
Choose the alternative with a correct order. now/books/on/ studying/out/of/is/print/of/the/one/best
o: Books on studying out of print is now one of the best.
Now books on studying out of print is one of the best.
One of the best books on studying is now out of print.
Studying on books now is one of the best out of print.
g12-english.e: Option A arranges the words into a grammatically correct and coherent declarative sentence: 'One of the best books on studying is now out of print.' (1)

g12-english.t: When the thief saw the police officers. It is face went as white as a sheet.
g12-english.e: "As white as a sheet" describes a face that has lost its colour, and blood drains from the face in fear. A thief who has caught sight of police officers is frightened, so terrified is the meaning. B is tempting because any strong feeling can change a face, but excitement usually brings colour to it, and there is nothing pleasant here for the thief.

g12-english.t: Ararso: What is your opinion about the need for college education? Jirata: ___________________
o: What is the requirement to join college?
I feel certain that it's absolutely necessary.
None of my children joined college.
I think I've a good idea about it.
g12-english.e: Ararso asks for an opinion on the need for college education, and Jirata directly expresses a strong opinion: 'I feel certain that it's absolutely necessary.'

g12-english.t: We ______ study in small groups when we were in the secondary school.
g12-english.e: The semi-modal structure 'used to + infinitive' is used to describe past habits or states that no longer occur in the present.

g12-english.t: I ______ I studied harder in school.
g12-english.e: The verb 'wish' is a stative verb used in the simple present tense ('I wish') to express a present regret about a past situation.

g12-english.t:
There appears to be an amendment made to the investment policy. However, we are not sure of who the major
___________________ is.
g12-english.e: A 'beneficiary' is a noun referring to a person or group that gains an advantage or profit from something, such as a policy change.

g12-english.t: As a parent, I have the discretion to determine which TV programs my children may watch.
g12-english.e: Having the 'discretion' to decide something means having the individual authority or 'right' to make that choice.

g12-english.t: Friend: You: It's Ok. It's enough to live on
g12-english.e: The response 'It's enough to live on' refers to income or salary, which directly answers the question 'How much do you earn?'.

g12-english.t: On my way home from office, there was high traffic ________. It took me two hours to get home.
g12-english.e: 'Traffic congestion' is the standard collocation used to describe heavy, slow-moving traffic that causes delays.

g12-english.t: Many more books ___ for the school library next year.
g12-english.e: The subject 'Many more books' is passive (books do not buy themselves), and the time indicator 'next year' requires the future passive form 'will be bought'.

g12-english.t: It ( in par 4) refers to
g12-english.e: 'It' is used as a subject pronoun referring to the main subject of the discussion, which is Aesop's fable.

g12-english.t: Supervisor: _____? There are errors of all kind in your essay. Student: Sorry, I'll proofread it before I hand it in.
o: Could you tell me about your writing
Are there errors of any kind in your essay
Do you care about your writing
Am I going to hate your writing
g12-english.e: The supervisor's critical remark about the errors is most logically preceded by asking "Do you care about your writing?", prompting the student's apologetic response.

g12-english.t: Lensa, who is always worried about her weight, eats like a/an ______
g12-english.e: "To eat like a bird" means to eat very little, which fits somebody who is always worried about her weight. C is the trap because "eat like a pig" is the better known idiom, but it means to eat a lot and greedily, which is the opposite of what the sentence sets up.

g12-english.t: any to don't us seem more understand they.
o: They seem to don't understand us any more.
Any more they don't seem to understand us.
To understand us they don't seem any more.
They don't seem to understand us any more.
g12-english.e: Option B follows proper English word order with the negative auxiliary verb preceding the main verb: 'They don't seem to understand us any more.' (1)

g12-english.t:
I didn't ring off until he said he didn't love me. Once i heard that, i forced myself to completely erase him out of
my mind.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'ring off' means to end a telephone conversation by putting the receiver down, which is synonymous with 'hang up'.

g12-english.t: Which of the following words can be synonymous with the word content as used in paragraph 6?
g12-english.e: The word 'content' as an adjective is a direct synonym of 'satisfied', which means pleased and easy in mind.

g12-english.t:
A : Do you mind if I ride your bicycle?
B : __________ It’s broken
g12-english.e: Answering 'Yes, I do' to a 'Do you mind' question means 'Yes, I do mind (and would prefer you didn't)', which makes sense here because the bicycle is broken.

g12-english.t: I understand it is taking them years to________________ the shock of their son's death. I really pity them.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'get over' means to recover from a shock, illness, or emotional trauma.

g12-english.t:
Practice has shown us that conflicts __________ occur here and there in the country and unfortunately we lost
thousands of lives.
g12-english.e: The modal 'will' is used to express general truths or predictable characteristic behaviors (things that are known to happen regularly based on practice).

g12-english.t:
We should teach children to _________ when they cross roads. There could be speeding vehicles coming from
either direction.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'look out' means to watch out or be vigilant, which is crucial when crossing roads to avoid speeding vehicles.

g12-english.t: ____________ need further clarification, give us a call or pay us a visit. We will be happy to assist.
g12-english.e: 'Should you' is an inverted conditional structure equivalent to 'If you should', which is used to make formal offers of assistance.

g12-english.t:
Wheel chair user: Could you tell me where the computer center is on this building? You : Oh sure, the 3rd room
from here _______ Wheel chair user : Thank you indeed.
o: Leave your wheelchair in my office.
Don't leave your wheelchair in my office.
Oh sure, the 3rd room from here.
Can I help you push the wheelchair?
g12-english.e: Since the interlocutor is a wheelchair user, offering assistance by asking 'Can I help you push the wheelchair?' is polite and matches their grateful response: 'Thank you indeed.'

g12-english.t: Kosif: I have a job interview after tomorrow. Naftai: ________________
o: If you dress smartly, you’ll impress them.
How long have you been jobless?
I know many people looking for a job.
g12-english.e: Providing encouraging advice like 'If you dress smartly, you'll impress them' is the most supportive, polite, and natural response to a friend who has an upcoming job interview.

g12-english.t: I found it difficult ___________the content of the lecturer’s explanation at university.
g12-english.e: The construction 'find it + adjective' is followed by a 'to-infinitive' ('to understand').

g12-english.t:
Friend: your cousin has just told me he's getting married next week are you very pleased? you: ________, but he
could have told me earlier.
o: where is the wedding to be held
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'but' introduces a minor complaint, meaning the first clause must answer the friend's question affirmatively with a positive sentiment like 'I'm absolutely delighted'.

g12-english.t: Teacher: what time do you go to bed? Student: __________________
g12-english.e: A direct question asking 'What time...?' expects a specific clock time as the answer, making 'At ten o'clock' the best choice.

g12-english.t: Adam:__________________ Mary: my pleasure. Just tell me what you want.
o: Could you buy me a battery for my watch?
Shall I tell you a secret?
Could you do me a favour, please?
Can I use your camera, please?
g12-english.e: 'Could you do me a favour, please?' is the standard request that prompts Mary's willing reply, 'My pleasure. Just tell me what you want.'

g12-english.t: According to the authors one of those given below is recommended to help deal with climate change.
g12-english.e: Prioritizing environmental rehabilitation (such as reforestation and soil conservation) is a primary and highly recommended national strategy to tackle climate change in Ethiopia.

g12-english.t:
Conflicts ________ take place between the pastoralists and farmers in this area every time the dry season
comes. The government has to find a means of solving the shortage of water which is the main cause of the
problem.
g12-english.e: The modal 'will' is used here to express typical or habitual behavior in the present under specific conditions ('every time the dry season comes'). (1)

g12-english.t: The use of real life situations made the activity so interactive that everyone in the class loved it.
g12-english.e: An 'interactive' activity involves active participation from everyone, making 'participatory' the most suitable synonym.

g12-english.t:
The words below are NOT in the proper order. When put in the right order, they make a correct English sentence.
Choose the alternative with a correct order. environment/a/of/affect/can/quality/polluted/our/a
o: A polluted quality environment of our life can affect.
A polluted can environment affect our quality of life.
A polluted environment can affect our quality of life.
A polluted affect environment of quality can our life.
g12-english.e: Option B forms a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence: 'A polluted environment can affect our quality of life.'

g12-english.t:
Abush: _____________________________________________
Friend: My dream is actually to visit Japan. The cleanliness attract me.
o: Which place in the world do you want to visit?
Which place in the world do you like most?
Which country in the world is attractive you.
Which country are you planning to visit?
g12-english.e: The friend's response refers to a 'dream to visit' a place, which matches the question 'Which place in the world do you want to visit?'

g12-english.t:
The house _______ into last night and they have already reported it to the police. I'll try to follow up the
progress.
g12-english.e: The sentence requires the past simple passive ('was broken') because the action took place at a specific time in the past ('last night') and the focus is on the house receiving the action of the verb.

g12-english.t: __________ in the town could you find any safe haven. I ask you to leave before it is too late.
g12-english.e: The negative adverb 'Nowhere' triggers subject-verb inversion ('could you find') when placed at the beginning of a sentence.

g12-english.t: Bontu: inflation is still on the rise in this country. Don't you think so? Chaltu:___________________
o: What did you buy these days?
I am afraid, it is not.
Is that still a double digit?
g12-english.e: 'Don't you think so?' asks for an opinion or agreement; 'I am afraid, it is not' politely expresses disagreement with the statement that inflation is on the rise.

g12-english.t:
Journalist: Thank you, Wolzero Hirut, for giving me the chance to ask you a few questions about your
organization. Wolzero Hirut: ____________
o: What is it this time? You were here last year, weren't you?
Okay. Go head. What do you want to know?
I have a meeting in an hour. Make it quick, please!
It's my pleasure and thank you for visiting us.
g12-english.e: In a formal interview, 'It's my pleasure and thank you for visiting us' is the most polite, professional, and welcoming response to a journalist's thanks.
