g12-english.t: You: Why should they go at this time of the year? Friend: ________, the weather is great now.
g12-english.e: 'To give you an idea' is used to provide an explanation or context, explaining why going at this time of the year makes sense due to the great weather.

g12-english.t: We don't want to eat fatty food anymore __________ it is said to be among the diet causing heart problems.
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'since' is used here to introduce a subordinate clause explaining the reason ('because it is said to be...').

g12-english.t: Doctors_________________ help you unless you tell them what's worng.
g12-english.e: In a real present conditional with 'unless' ('unless you tell them'), the main clause uses 'can't' to express present inability.

g12-english.t: Teachers should _______ the attitude of honesty and integrity in the minds of their learners.
g12-english.e: One 'cultivates' an attitude or mental quality in others, meaning to foster or grow it over time through teaching and practice. (1)

g12-english.t:
Being, submissive is usually interpreted very negatively by many people. Others, however, claim that this can
sometimes make people kind to you.
g12-english.e: The adjective 'docile' means ready to accept control or instruction, making it a direct synonym for 'submissive'.

g12-english.t:
Your room is still _________! Remember, I told you to get your stuff organized when I visited you last time. If I
found the same next time, make sure you would be out.
g12-english.e: The request to get 'stuff organized' indicates that the room is currently cluttered or 'untidy'.

g12-english.t:
As the company is new, we will need to produce some kind of ______________ to be distributed to the
community around.
g12-english.e: A 'leaflet' is a printed sheet of paper containing information or advertising that is specifically designed to be distributed to people in a community

g12-english.t: before were in they a all packed room interrogation tiny started.
o: Interrogation were started before they all packed in a tiny room.
Before they were packed started all interrogation in a tiny room.
All packed in a tiny room before they were started interrogation.
They were all packed in a tiny room before interrogation started.
g12-english.e: Arranging the words in the order of Option B produces 'They were all packed in a tiny room before interrogation started', which is the only coherent and grammatically correct sentence.

g12-english.t: I have searched all over and______________could it be found. Someone must have thrown ot out.
g12-english.e: The negative adverb 'nowhere' placed at the front of the clause causes subject-auxiliary inversion ('could it be found').

g12-english.t:
The fundraising project in our kebele has been more successful than ever before. An insider told me
they_________ raise 10 million birr in six months.
g12-english.e: 'Were able to' is used to talk about achieving a specific, difficult task on a particular past occasion, which fits the successful completion of the fundraising target.

g12-english.t: Obang: My computer has suddenly shut down. What has happened to it? Technician: __________________
o: Mine has never been like that.
Is that a very old computer?
I hope that wouldn't be a virus.
Were you typing stuff on it?
g12-english.e: A technician would logically speculate on the cause of a sudden shutdown, making 'I hope that wouldn't be a virus' a suitable diagnostic response.

g12-english.t:
The new prime minister seems to have the _________ of a natural leader. But to be successful, he needs the
cooperation of all the people.
g12-english.e: 'Dynamism' is the noun that describes the quality of being characterized by vigorous activity and progress, which perfectly describes the positive traits of a natural leader. (1)

g12-english.t: He has secured his visa and everything necessary for his travel. They say he_____________move to the USA.
g12-english.e: 'Is going to' expresses an intention or a plan that has already been arranged and prepared, evidenced by securing the visa and travel necessities.

g12-english.t:
Everybody was unusually punctual. There was, however, someone very important that was still expected the
driver. While everyone was eagerly waiting to leave the campus, Samuel's phone range. It was the driver.....This is
taken from a piece of writing that is most likely:
g12-english.e: The paragraph tells a story by describing a situation and an unfolding event ('While everyone was eagerly waiting... Samuel's phone rang'), which is the hallmark of narrative writing.

g12-english.t: _________ prices are still on the rise, we hope they will come down in the near future.
g12-english.e: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a clause of concession, showing contrast between rising prices and the hope that they will come down.

g12-english.t: You_______ try paying them more money to get the job done.
g12-english.e: The modal verb 'should' is used here to offer a suggestion or advice on how to get the job done.

g12-english.t: ___________________ You come around, i see you making troubles. That is really intolerable.
g12-english.e: 'Every time' acts as a subordinating conjunction meaning 'whenever', linking the clause 'you come around' to the main clause.

g12-english.t: Workers in big firms receive a substantial part of their pay in the form of attractive bonuses and overtime.
g12-english.e: The word 'substantial' means of considerable importance, size, or worth.

g12-english.t:
I just heard on the radio that the company is selling goods at a big discount. I___________________ go and
check if there is anything i might need.
g12-english.e: We use 'will' for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking (upon just hearing the news).

g12-english.t: I wish that we _______ today. It is really freezing and wet.
g12-english.e: To express a regret or wish about a present situation ('today'), the past simple subjunctive ('didn't need to work') is used after 'wish'.

g12-english.t: Nana: Dad is getting us a new TV set. I am excited. Chala: _____________.
o: Many people around do not have a TV set.
How much is he going to pay?
g12-english.e: Nana shares good news and says she is excited, so the reply should share the feeling. "I can't believe that!" is the surprised, pleased reaction news like this expects. B is the trap because it is a question about the family's money, which turns a happy announcement into something uncomfortable.

g12-english.t: From the excerpts below A-D, identify the one stated in a formal register
o: Good morning, Mr. Tsegaye. How are you today?
Are you gonna to Friendship Park tomorrow?
Yeah, I am okay. And you?
g12-english.e: Formal register uses a full greeting, a title with the family name, and complete words. D has all three: Good morning, Mr. Tsegaye. How are you today? Hi, Yeah and gonna are marks of informal spoken English, so A, B and C are casual. Rule: Formal writing avoids short forms and slang, and uses titles such as Mr., Mrs. and Dr.

g12-english.t: My friend took out a ___ from a bank to buy a house, but he could not pay it back in time.
g12-english.e: To borrow money from a bank to purchase property is to take out a 'loan'.

g12-english.t: All my friends wanted coffee so I_______________them some.
g12-english.e: The sentence describes a completed past action matching the past tense in the first clause ('wanted coffee so I made them some').

g12-english.t: The interviewee impressed the committee, __________?
g12-english.e: For a positive statement in the past simple ('impressed'), the correct question tag is negative and uses the auxiliary 'did' ('didn't he').

g12-english.t: Nurse: __________________ Patient: Do i have to ?
o: Sleep well. I wish you good dreams.
g12-english.e: When asked 'Have you taken your medicine?', a reluctant patient would respond with 'Do I have to [take it]?' to question the necessity of doing so.

g12-english.t:
I am writing to express my disappointment with the Samsung television I purchased from your store on January
15, 2025 (Receipt #2345). The screen developed dark lines within two weeks of purchase. This letter is most
likely a/an:
g12-english.e: The writer names a disappointment, the product, the date of purchase, the receipt number and the fault that appeared. Writing to a shop about a faulty product is a complaint. Option C, an apology letter, would come from the side at fault, and here the writer is the buyer.

g12-english.t:
You don't seem to have ever seen the creature __________ I told you about. It looked nothing like a kangaroo
except in the way it walked.
g12-english.e: The relative pronoun 'which' (or 'that') is used to refer to non-human entities like 'the creature'.

g12-english.t:
If you don't tell the truth, they __________ keep you jailed forever. Better say that you killed him in defense of
yourself and you may be paroled.
g12-english.e: This is a First Conditional sentence ('If you don't tell... they will keep...'), where 'will' expresses a certain future consequence of a real possibility.

g12-english.t: Student: We went to Sodere for the weekend. Teacher________________?
g12-english.e: The student already stated both the destination ('Sodere') and the time ('the weekend'), so asking 'What for?' is the only logical follow-up to learn the purpose of the trip.

g12-english.t: If he ___ more carefully, he wouldn't have had the accident.
g12-english.e: This is a third conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical past situation. The structure requires 'If' + past perfect ('had driven') in the condition clause, and 'would have' + past participle in the consequence clause. (1)

g12-english.t: Many accidents occur_______ drivers are often reckless.
g12-english.e: The subordinating conjunction 'because' is used to introduce the clause that gives the reason why many accidents occur.

g12-english.t:
Of all the stuff she bought yesterday, I like the books ______________ she got from the library. I started reading
one of them and the story is really thrilling.
g12-english.e: The relative pronoun 'which' is used to refer to things or objects, such as 'the books', in a relative clause. (1)

g12-english.t: a take half it one days to may and cure.
o: It may take to cure one and a half days.
It may take one and half days to a cure.
It may take a one and half days to cure.
It may take one and a half days to cure.
g12-english.e: The scrambled words are correctly arranged to form the grammatically and semantically sound sentence: 'It may take one and a half days to cure.'

g12-english.t:
Chief: I think we should leave. I didn't like the atmosphere. Yared: ____________ things seem to be changing for
positive. Let's wait a bit.
o: I agree up to a point, but
Even though that is the case
g12-english.e: 'I agree up to a point, but' is used to politely acknowledge the chief's concern about the atmosphere while presenting a counter-argument to wait.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following is NOT implied in what the author states reasons for diversity?
o: The social origin of the individual
The kind of people one met in life
The kind of family one comes from
g12-english.e: While family, social origin, and personal associations are external factors/reasons that shape diversity (nurture), one's behavioral characteristics are the outcome or expression of that diversity, rather than its cause.

g12-english.t: my actions and the trouble I have caused..." this is likely taken from a letter of__________________
g12-english.e: Acknowledging one's own negative actions and expressing regret for the trouble caused is characteristic of a letter of apology.

g12-english.t:
You: i always have trouble with my English. What do you advise me to do? Friend:
___________________________
o: Have you thought about seeing a doctor?
g12-english.e: When unable to provide the requested advice, a speaker politely expresses regret using 'I wish I could help.'

g12-english.t: Yodit: we're going out for lunch. Would you come? Sara: ________________
o: I am afraid, we have no money.
Who is going for lunch now?
I would rather do it for dinner.
g12-english.e: Sara politely expresses a preference for an alternative time ('I would rather do it for dinner') in response to Yodit's lunch invitation.

g12-english.t: Children using the swimming pool must be ________ by an adult at all times.
g12-english.e: 'Accompanied by' means to be escorted or joined by someone, which is the standard safety requirement for children at a swimming pool.

g12-english.t: You ___________ furious I haven't seen you presenting like this before.
g12-english.e: 'Must be' is used to make a logical deduction based on strong present evidence.

g12-english.t: Aster: Is he your husband? I haven't met him before. Lidya: Come on, ________ How dare you?
g12-english.e: Lidya's response 'How dare you?' indicates she finds Aster's question or insinuation offensive, and 'what do you mean?' perfectly expresses this indignation.

g12-english.t:
She will have to see the manager __________ she arrives. I heard he is going to send her to the new branch in
Gambella.
g12-english.e: 'As soon as' is a temporal conjunction meaning 'immediately after', which perfectly fits the timeline of her arrival and meeting the manager.

g12-english.t:
The fact is that I didn't know she was in such a serious problem. Now you calm down and I ____________ do
everything possible. OK?
g12-english.e: The modal 'will' is used to express a spontaneous decision or promise made at the moment of speaking, such as offering immediate assistance.

g12-english.t: Physical labor can exhaust the body; ________. excessive reading can reduce mental power.
g12-english.e: 'Equally' is used here as a transition showing a parallel or equivalent effect between physical labor exhausting the body and excessive reading fatiguing the mind.

g12-english.t:
The AU meeting to be held next month is expected to pass resolutions pertaining to the relationship between
the two warring parties. We are looking forward to it.
g12-english.e: An official meeting of heads of state or high-level representatives, such as the African Union (AU) meeting, is called a 'summit'.

g12-english.t: Samson: How much coffee do you drink? Tewodros:_______________.
g12-english.e: The question 'How much coffee do you drink?' asks for a quantity, which is appropriately answered by 'at least five cups'.

g12-english.t: Committing corruption_______ life imprisonment in several countries in the world.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'leads to' means 'results in' or 'causes', which fits the context of corruption resulting in imprisonment.

g12-english.t: I was with her for dinner. She _______________ the car which they claim disappeared around 7 pm.
g12-english.e: The first sentence is an alibi: the speaker was with her at dinner, so she was not able to take the car at the time it disappeared. That denial of ability is "couldn't". B is the trap because "would have stolen" is also about the past, but it asserts that she did it, which contradicts the alibi the speaker has given.

g12-english.t: Speaking on the phone, if you press the red button, the call ______.
g12-english.e: This is a zero conditional sentence (expressing a general rule or fact), which uses the simple present tense ('ends') in the main clause.

g12-english.t:
Yihun: Poor Lili! She lost all her money.
Jember: ________________________________
g12-english.e: 'What a pity! How come?' is a natural response that shows empathy for someone's misfortune and asks for elaboration.

g12-english.t:
Bertukan: My new boyfriend loves me a lot.
Mamitu: ___________________________
o: Isn't that rather too soon to say?
Did you break up with Temesgen?
He is very handsome, isn't he?
g12-english.e: Since the boyfriend is 'new', Mamitu's skeptical response ('Isn't that rather too soon to say?') is a natural and conversational reaction to the claim that he already loves her a lot.

g12-english.t: These people are so mean that they hardly give anything to charity. They are different from the other village
g12-english.e: In British and general English, 'mean' often describes someone who is tight-fisted or unwilling to share or give money to others, closely meaning 'selfish' or ungenerous.

g12-english.t:
Why are you worried about her? I know she is capable . Just leave her alone and you will see how beautifully she 
would do it.
g12-english.e: "Capable" means having the ability, fitness, or quality necessary to do something, which is synonymous with "competent".

g12-english.t: The police arrested the man who often has his lunch at this afternoon and makes off .
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'make off' means to hurry away, especially in order to escape, which corresponds to 'leaves in haste'. (1)

g12-english.t:
I __________ this job for the last 35 years and I don't think I would even think of changing it. It is my world and I
feel there is no better world for me.
g12-english.e: The present perfect 'have done' is used with 'for the last 35 years' to indicate an activity that began in the past and continues to the present moment. (1)

g12-english.t: Look! The sky is cloudy and __________ to get your T-shirts in.
g12-english.e: The verb 'hope' is grammatically followed by a 'to-infinitive' ('I hope to get your T-shirts in'), whereas 'think', 'feel', and 'know' do not fit this grammatical structure in this context.

g12-english.t:
They had to get together at six in the morning and when we got up at 5:45 a.m, we thought we wouldn't make it. 
However, we ________________________ to get there before they left.
g12-english.e: 'Were able' is used to express successful performance of a specific action in the past, especially when overcoming difficulties.

g12-english.t: ________ by the speech of the new leader, all the people of the Zone elected him to be Member of Parliament.
g12-english.e: The fact that the people elected him to the parliament indicates they were positively moved and 'inspired' by his speech.

g12-english.t: Olonso: Is everything ready? They’re coming this Sunday. Melana: ________________
o: Sunday is a day of worship, of course.
I doubt they’ve changed their schedule.
Do you think you’ll be here on Sunday?
Let’s hope they’ll bring us some clothes.
g12-english.e: In response to a question about readiness for guests arriving on Sunday, Melana's assurance that she expects them on schedule ('I doubt they’ve changed their schedule') is the most relevant and logical answer. (1)

g12-english.t: Which of the following can be the best title for the passage?
g12-english.e: "Recycling Paper" is the most suitable title because the text focuses on the environmental impacts of paper production and how recycling helps mitigate them.

g12-english.t:
Heavy shellings in several cities of Syria have turned buildings into rubbles. It would obviously take a lot of
resource to reconstruct them
g12-english.e: 'Rubble' refers to the broken fragments or remains of destroyed buildings, which is synonymous with 'debris'.

g12-english.t: Customer: I'd like to withdraw 5,000 Birr, please. Cashier: ____________________?
o: Could you write your name here, please
How would you like the money
Do you want to make a withdrawal
What is the interest rate on your account
g12-english.e: "How would you like the money?" is the standard question a cashier asks a customer who is making a cash withdrawal, referring to the preferred bill denominations.

g12-english.t: Funny in (par2) means
g12-english.e: 'Funny' is defined as causing laughter or amusement.

g12-english.t:
Never lose hope and don't stop your struggle. You will, one day, come out ___________ and put to shame all
those who told you would see no success.
g12-english.e: Coming out 'triumphant' means achieving victory or success, which perfectly contrasts with and puts to shame those who predicted failure. (1)

g12-english.t:
Despite the provocative comments made by some of her audience, she chose her words very carefully
__________ not to go out of topic and make the issue personal. I really admired her patience.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'so as not to' is the correct negative infinitive of purpose, used to show the intention behind choosing her words carefully.

g12-english.t: Next time you come to class don't forget to ___ your textbook.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'don't forget to' is followed by the bare infinitive of the verb, which is 'bring' (since 'to' is already provided in the sentence template). (1)

g12-english.t:
After her long career in several international organizations, she is now engaged in humanitarian service
intending to give back to the community.
g12-english.e: Humanitarian services focus on helping people and improving human welfare, which is synonymous with 'charitable' work.

g12-english.t:
Surafel: They should know that we can't help them because we don't have the time. Tolera:
______________________
o: Besides, we don't have the required resources.
We can find out the information from our friend.
They insist on going out for dinner this evening.
We don't clearly know why he is so interested in the matter.
g12-english.e: Surafel explains they cannot help because of a lack of time. Tolera supports this explanation by adding another constraint ('Besides, we don't have the required resources') using the transition word 'besides'. (1)

g12-english.t:
Ziyad: I hear they provide free lunch here. Mukerem: No! ________________________, nobody will do the public
works.
g12-english.e: The conditional 'If there is free lunch, nobody will do...' represents a realistic first conditional situation expressing the speaker's concern.

g12-english.t:
'Love is a very powerful force; it conquers barriers of color, race, religion, and culture. It thrives on mutual
nurturing of each other,' it is very likely that the writing is:
g12-english.e: The excerpt explains and defines the abstract concept of love and its characteristics. Explaining or defining a topic is the primary purpose of expository writing.

g12-english.t:
Mebratu: What are the primary stages of coffee preparation? Rukya: First, we wash, roast and ground coffee
beans. ______, we add the coffee powder into the kettle.
g12-english.e: The participle phrase 'Having done this' functions as a transition, meaning 'after washing, roasting, and grinding coffee beans'.

g12-english.t:
II. Language Focus (Questions 33–65)
You had better ______ an umbrella. It looks like it will rain.
g12-english.e: "Had better" is followed by the base form of the verb (infinitive without "to"). "You had better take an umbrella." We never use "to" after "had better" or "would rather."

g12-english.t: If the police men had not been carrying a gun, he could not have killed the criminal.
o: The policeman wasn't carrying a gun and he didn't kill the criminal
The policeman was carrying a gun but he was not able to kill the criminal.
The policeman was not carrying a gun.
The policeman was carrying a gun.
g12-english.e: This third conditional sentence ("If + past perfect..., could have...") describes a hypothetical scenario that is the opposite of what actually happened. Thus, the implication is that the policeman was carrying a gun and killed the criminal.

g12-english.t:
Apparently there are lots of buildings in Addis Ababa that should be, _________ because of their inferior quality.
If left alone, they could be risky to the occupants.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'pulled down' means to demolish a building, which is necessary for structures of inferior quality to prevent them from collapsing on occupants.

g12-english.t:
Robel: It's our friend's wedding this coming Sunday, so I'll have my hair done tomorrow. What about you? Genet:
________. We should look our best on this great day!
g12-english.e: To agree with a positive future statement ('I'll have my hair done...'), the structure 'So will I' is used. 'Neither' and 'Nor' are used to agree with negative statements.

g12-english.t: Teacher: Today I'm going to tell you about AI. Student: ________ Teacher: AI, meaning Artificial Intelligence.
o: I didn't hold that. Could you repeat that, please?
I didn't catch that. Could you repeat that, please?
I see I got your point.
You're speaking fast, but I can hear you.
g12-english.e: The student needs clarification of what 'AI' means. 'I didn't catch that. Could you repeat that, please?' is a standard English idiom used when one fails to hear or understand something.

g12-english.t:
AIDS patients used to be alienated for having HIV in their blood. Today, however, things have changed and they
are treated like any healthy person.
g12-english.e: To be 'alienated' or treated as an outcast due to a disease like HIV/AIDS is synonymous with being 'stigmatized'.

g12-english.t:
Many of my friends were in heated argument about which team would win the game last night; in fact, i was
______________ and simply enjoyed watching the game.
g12-english.e: 'Indifferent' means having no preference or biased interest in the outcome, contrasting with friends engaged in a heated argument.

g12-english.t:
We all contributed what is within our reach ________________ help the needy children in our school. We bought 
them the stationery they needed for the whole year.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'so as to' is used to express purpose followed by a bare infinitive ('help').

g12-english.t: Eldana: it is time we left. It is going to rain later. Friend:________________i_ don 't want to get my hair wet.
g12-english.e: "I couldn't agree more" expresses strong agreement with Eldana's recommendation to leave before the rain starts. (1)

g12-english.t: Thomas: Constant use of social media leads to low reading habits. Gebre: ______________.
o: I have the right to say that
g12-english.e: The phrase 'I agree with you entirely' is a standard and polite way of expressing total agreement with another person's opinion in a conversation.

g12-english.t: Ethiopia is working hard towards strengthening its ______ relations with many countries.
g12-english.e: 'Diplomatic' relations refers to the formal relations maintained between nations, which fits the context of Ethiopia's international efforts. (1)

g12-english.t:
This year, money _________ for the construction of a wider and greener football pitch. The school management
has decided to improve the sports field in our school.
g12-english.e: The noun 'money' is the receiver of the action, so the passive voice is required; 'is being raised' indicates an ongoing action happening 'this year'.

g12-english.t: Who does ' our ' as used in Paragraph 1 Line 1 refer to?
g12-english.e: The term 'our' refers to human beings, as the passage discusses chimpanzees being our closest living evolutionary relatives, sharing over 98% of our DNA.

g12-english.t:
We were worried that everybody had very little money left. It was even more frustrating that Abdu, our group
leader, had the __________ compared to the rest of us.
g12-english.e: The superlative adjective 'least' is correct because it is preceded by the definite article 'the' and compares Abdu's money to that of everyone else in the group.

g12-english.t:
The smell of fresh 'doro wat' and bread was omnipresent in the neighbourhood during the holidays. We used to
enjoy it by moving here and there when we were in our country. (omnipresent means)
g12-english.e: The sentence says the smell filled the neighbourhood during the holidays and that people moved about enjoying it. Omnipresent means present in every place. Option C, very inaccessible, would mean hard to reach, which is the opposite of a smell you meet wherever you go.

g12-english.t: Interviewer: ______ Interviewee: I applied for the position of Business Manager.
o: With which skills are you most comfortable?
What position are you looking for?
g12-english.e: The interviewee's response directly names the job position they applied for, which answers 'What position are you looking for?'

g12-english.t: I always believe it is healthy for everyone to repress their emotions.
g12-english.e: To 'repress' emotions means to restrain or suppress them, which corresponds directly to the phrasal verb 'hold back'.

g12-english.t: I don't like people who beat around the bush. I want them to...
o: stop blaming others for their own mistakes
g12-english.e: To beat around the bush is to talk around a subject instead of saying the point. So the speaker wants people to stop avoiding the issue. Option B is tempting because of the word bush, but the idiom blames the speaker for hiding the point, not the listener for hunting it.

g12-english.t: am / as / think / I / not / I / you / stupid / am / as
o: I am not as stupid as you think I am.
As you think I am not stupid as I am.
I am not as I think am stupid as you.
I am not as you think as I am.
g12-english.e: This option organizes the words into the grammatically and logically coherent sentence: 'I am not as stupid as you think I am.'

g12-english.t: often / to quite/I/ dream/ my job.
o: I often dream to quit my job.
my job often dream to quit.
I dream often to quit my job.
I quit my job to dream
g12-english.e: The scrambled words are correctly arranged in option D to form the grammatical sentence 'I often dream to quit my job' (correcting the typo 'quite' to 'quit').

g12-english.t: Student: are we having an exam next week? Teacher:________________
o: Your result last time was so good.
How many units have we done?
I am not sure yet, but you might.
g12-english.e: The student asks a direct yes/no question about the possibility of an exam, and the teacher appropriately answers with their current state of planning: "I am not sure yet, but you might."

g12-english.t: Mesele: It seems we are in a difficult time at the moment. Kuma: _______________________
o: Please arrive here as early as you can
I believe the situation will improve soon.
g12-english.e: Kuma's response 'I believe the situation will improve soon' is a logical, reassuring, and cohesive reply to Mesele's observation about being in a difficult time.

g12-english.t: I was _______ scared to go out in the dark alone. That is why I couldn't join you for dinner.
g12-english.e: 'Absolutely' is used as an intensifier with adjectives to show a high degree of emotion (e.g., 'absolutely scared'). (1)

g12-english.t: The teacher asked us to hand in the homework this Friday.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'hand in' means to give or submit completed work to a person in authority, such as a teacher.

g12-english.t: On her return from a trip, she got an accident resulting in the amputation on her right leg.
g12-english.e: The amputation of a limb results in a permanent physical 'impairment' or disability. (1)

g12-english.t: ______________ telephones first appeared they were called talking telegraphs.
g12-english.e: The subordinating conjunction 'When' is used to introduce the adverbial clause of time in this sentence.

g12-english.t: In a formal letter the recipient's address will be
o: at the bottom of the letter.
in the top right hand corner.
g12-english.e: In the standard business letter the sender's own address comes first, then the date, and then the address of the person receiving the letter, on the left. So the recipient's address sits below the sender's address. The top right corner belongs to the sender's address, and nothing about the address goes at the foot of the letter.

g12-english.t: My friend says that she ______ all her assignments already.
g12-english.e: The present perfect tense 'has done' is used with 'already' to indicate a completed action reported in the present tense ('says').

g12-english.t: Ato Bisrat has been ______________chairman of the new committee.
g12-english.e: 'Appointed' means officially assigned or chosen for a job or position of responsibility, such as committee chairman.

g12-english.t: Pen: Write; Rubber: __________
g12-english.e: The relationship is tool to function: a pen is used to write, and a rubber (eraser) is used to erase.

g12-english.t: If a chairperson's argument is nebulous in the meeting, it will confuse the participants.
g12-english.e: 'Nebulous' means vague, ill-defined, or unclear, which naturally leads to confusion among participants.

g12-english.t: I know I was______________ in the field, but not exactly where.
g12-english.e: 'Somewhere' is used in affirmative sentences to indicate an unspecified or unknown location, fitting the phrase 'not exactly where'.

g12-english.t: Kenubish: It is heavily cloudy. Do you think we can go? Kenan: ________________ Let’s make it some other day.
o: Rain means green. You should really be happy.
It looks as if it is going to rain.
You know we’ve been in the whole day.
g12-english.e: Kenan's suggestion to postpone ('Let's make it some other day') supports the observation that 'It looks as if it is going to rain' due to the heavy clouds.

g12-english.t: The man says that he can beat anybody in a fight, but actually he is cowardly bully.
g12-english.e: The word 'cowardly' describes someone who lacks courage, which is synonymous with 'timid'.

g12-english.t: __________I do not complain much; my friends often take me for a fool.
g12-english.e: The subordinating conjunction 'Because' is used to introduce a clause of reason ('I do not complain much') that explains the main clause.

g12-english.t:
Ethiopia will enjoy a period of peace and ________ in the next few years; this happens if the country ensures
law and gives priority to science, technology and innovation.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'peace and prosperity' is a common English collocation that fits the positive future predicted for the country.

g12-english.t: The organization's new group of trucks has just arrived after ten days' journey from the port.
g12-english.e: A 'fleet' is the correct collective noun used to describe a group of vehicles, ships, or trucks operating together. (1)

g12-english.t:
Your persistent complaints have now started to irritate me. How come that your eyes cannot see anything
positive of what is going on?
g12-english.e: The verb "irritate" means to make someone annoyed, impatient, or angry.

g12-english.t:
Any country needs a strong government in order to limit or eradicate unlawful activities by some elements of
society.
g12-english.e: 'Illicit' means forbidden by law, rules, or custom, making it the perfect synonym for 'unlawful' activities.

g12-english.t:
"it is possible to see that parental influence has a significant impact on the academic performance and social
interaction of a child." Which section of a research report is this most likely taken from?
g12-english.e: The phrase 'it is possible to see that parental influence has a significant impact...' summarizes the overarching findings and implications of the study, which belongs in the Conclusion section.

g12-english.t: As mistake is to eraser so is constitution to ___________________
g12-english.e: An eraser is used to modify or correct a mistake, just as an amendment is used to modify or alter a constitution.

g12-english.t:
You know! __________ his diligence, you here nobody talking positively of him. I can't understand if the secret
behind is luck or lack.
g12-english.e: 'In spite of' is a prepositional phrase followed by a noun phrase ('his diligence'). Option B is incorrect because 'despite' is never followed by 'of', and Option D requires a full clause.

g12-english.t: My sister is such a little nuisance; she often like to ask too many silly questions.
g12-english.e: A 'nuisance' is a person, thing, or circumstance causing irritation or inconvenience, corresponding to 'annoying'.

g12-english.t:
We cannot interfere at the moment. He __________ and all we can do is wait until they finish it and see their
decision.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'at the moment' indicates a present ongoing action, and since the subject 'He' is receiving the action, the present continuous passive 'is being interrogated' is correct.

g12-english.t: What does the word ' demands ' as used in paragraph 4, line 5 mean?
g12-english.e: In an academic or institutional context, 'demands' refers to the rigorous standards or 'requirements' that must be met.

g12-english.t: I often can't stand people who always complain. They get on my nerve.
g12-english.e: The idiom 'can't stand' means to strongly dislike or be unable to tolerate someone or something.

g12-english.t: Mekbib: Excuse me, can you lend me a pencil? Zeritu: _________________
g12-english.e: 'Here you are' is the standard polite phrase used when handing someone an item they have requested to borrow. (1)

g12-english.t: He asked her to turn round several times before he gave her his opinion of her new dress.
g12-english.e: To 'turn round' means to rotate or spin around, allowing someone to view something from all angles.

g12-english.t: Mamusha: You've got a nice car. It looks great. Yaya: Sure, but _________
o: it is not as fast as yours
it is brand new straight from Japan
it is as fast as yours
it is not very good, I'm afraid
g12-english.e: The conjunction 'but' introduces a contrasting limitation about the car, making 'it is not as fast as yours' the most logical option when comparing it to the speaker's car.

g12-english.t: There is a need to assign an expert to wipe up unnecessary data from computer.
g12-english.e: 'Wipe up' (often used interchangeably with 'wipe out' or 'clean up' in computing context) means to remove or delete unnecessary data to free up space.

g12-english.t:
Aster: _____does your father do?
Regasa: He’s a teacher
g12-english.e: The question 'What does [someone] do?' is the standard way to ask about someone's occupation or job.

g12-english.t: Alem: The report is not comprehensive. Ululu:____________________
o: Sure. The language is really terrible.
I know, it is not easy to understand.
That is true. It has no focus at all.
Certainly. Send it back to her.
g12-english.e: Ululu agrees with Alem's evaluation that the report is inadequate (not comprehensive) and offers an appropriate course of action: "Certainly. Send it back to her."

g12-english.t:
Lensa: My spoken English is really horrible; ________________? Zemzem: Practice speaking every day in front
of your friends.
g12-english.e: Zemzem's response is a piece of advice ('Practice speaking every day...'), which directly answers Lensa's question asking for advice, 'what should I do?'. (1)

g12-english.t: Abebe: let us contribute to the building of the Renaissance Dam You:____________________
o: What is the position of Egypt now?
How much if it has been completed?
I was really proud when I visited it.
g12-english.e: 'Splendid! I can't agree more' expresses strong agreement with Abebe's suggestion to contribute to the dam project.

g12-english.t: Which of the following best replaces the word 'aggravated' in paragraph 2?
g12-english.e: The verb 'aggravated' means to make a problem or injury worse, so 'worsened' is the correct synonym.

g12-english.t: What does the word they (Para. 4) refer to?
g12-english.e: In her memoirs, she frequently refers to her teachers as her 'saviors' who opened up the world to her, making 'they' refer to her teachers.

g12-english.t: Breakfast to bread are have going for we.
o: We are going to have for breakfast bread.
We are for breakfast going to have bread.
We are going to have bread for breakfast.
We are going for bread to have breakfast.
g12-english.e: The standard English word order for this sentence is subject + be going to + verb + direct object + prepositional phrase: "We are going to have bread for breakfast."

g12-english.t:
Their plane is expected to land slightly after 3:00 pm. _______ it gets late, give me a call and I'll see what I can
do.
g12-english.e: 'In case' is used to talk about things we do in order to be prepared for possible future situations (e.g., calling if the plane gets late).

g12-english.t:
Some students develop a problem of______________________ to the university environment .They should be
properly counselled.
g12-english.e: The correct prefix to denote bad, faulty, or inadequate adjustment is 'mal-', forming the standard psychological and general English noun 'maladjustment'.

g12-english.t: Son: dad, can you tell me the year I was born? Dad: yes,__________________________
g12-english.e: The son asks for the year of his birth, and '2007' provides a specific year.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following phrases is similar in meaning to the phrase 'safe and beneficial' in paragraph 4?
g12-english.e: The phrase 'safe and beneficial' is synonymous with 'harmless and useful' because 'safe' means free from harm and 'beneficial' means producing good results or being useful.

g12-english.t: The police should heighten the awareness of the community in order to put
g12-english.e: To 'heighten' awareness means to increase or 'raise' it, making 'raise' the best synonym. (1)

g12-english.t:
A story written by a person about his/her experience of travelling from one place to another would most likely
be________________
g12-english.e: A story recounting personal experiences of travelling from one place to another in chronological order is a narrative. (1)

g12-english.t: There was a significant________ in crop production because of the shortage of rain.
g12-english.e: A shortage of rain naturally leads to a decrease or 'reduction' in agricultural crop production.

g12-english.t: Guest: the kitchen handle has come off. You: don't worry.________
o: it has never been like that
g12-english.e: Saying 'it often does' reassures the guest that the incident is a common occurrence and not their fault.

g12-english.t: I can't meet you these days I __________ my semester assignment which is due in two weeks' time.
g12-english.e: The future continuous 'will be doing' is used to describe an ongoing action that will occupy her time in the near future.

g12-english.t: Everybody suggested about the major causes of conflict, _____?
g12-english.e: Everybody is picked up by they in a question tag, and the main verb, suggested, is past simple, so the tag is didn't they. Option B uses weren't, which would need a form of be in the main clause, and there is none.

g12-english.t:
For any healthy business, there comes a point when the owners determine to take the _______________ of a
new growth strategy.
g12-english.e: "Take the risk" is a standard English collocation that means to do something although you know that something bad could happen, which fits the context of implementing a new growth strategy.

g12-english.t:
You shouldn't let your children ____________ in this pool. The water hasn't been decreased for the past four
months.
g12-english.e: The causative verb 'let' is followed by an object and a bare infinitive ('swim' without 'to').

g12-english.t: were the is stage that it high she time on.
o: It is high time that she were on the stage.
It is the stage that she were on high time.
She is on high time that were it the stage.
She is on high time that it were the stage.
g12-english.e: The fixed expression is It is high time + subject + past form of the verb, and it means the action is already late. So the sentence is It is high time that she were on the stage. The past form were here is not real past time; it is the unreal past, the same form used after I wish. The other options put she or the stage in the subject position, which breaks the expression. See Grade 12 English, Unit 9, verb patterns with wish.

g12-english.t:
Shumie: If you come from a poor family, you almost always end up poor. Nunu: No! ________________ His
parents were poor but he’s a millionaire.
o: If Mamo works hard, he’ll be OK.
Biru is not in the business industry.
g12-english.e: Nunu disagrees with Shumie's generalization and introduces Shola as a counterexample: 'Take, for example, Shola. His parents were poor but he’s a millionaire.'

g12-english.t:
Aster: Jim and Jane are marrying next week.
Beli: _____________________
o: I know Jim loves her, but she was going out with someone else.
There are so many weddings to take place next week.
Jane is so beautiful that all the boys around like her.
I don't think they would make a good couple.
g12-english.e: Expressing an opinion on whether the couple is well-suited ('I don't think they would make a good couple') is a very common conversational reaction to a wedding announcement. (1)

g12-english.t: Which one of the following is most likely an opening to your application for a job?
g12-english.e: "Dear Sir" is a traditional and highly appropriate formal salutation used when opening a job application letter when the recipient's name is unknown.

g12-english.t: There is no point in complaining about his immature behavior; he is always.
g12-english.e: 'Immature' behavior in adults is often described as 'childlike' or childish, as it resembles the behavior of a child.

g12-english.t: Writing a formal letter in English is not difficult, but you should follow certain_______________.
g12-english.e: 'Conventions' refers to widely accepted rules, norms, or practices, such as the standard format for formal letter writing.

g12-english.t: Yerom: may I give her my mobile phone? Wirtu:________________
o: Does she buy a mobile phone?
g12-english.e: 'No way! Are you crazy?' is a natural colloquial exclamation expressing strong objection to giving away a valuable personal item like a mobile phone.

g12-english.t: If you continue practising speaking English like this, you _______ speak it fluently very soon.
g12-english.e: In a first conditional sentence ('If + present simple'), the result clause expresses future ability using 'will be able to'.

g12-english.t:
Same passage
Which of the following words is used to suggest disapproval? (paragraph 6)
g12-english.e: The phrase 'with a sniff' is used to show disdain or disapproval, indicating that medics look down upon the term or concept of 'cyberchondria'.

g12-english.t: The lady ___________next to our English teacher is my mother's close friend.
g12-english.e: The present participle 'sitting' acts as a reduced relative clause (short for 'who is sitting') describing 'the lady'.

g12-english.t:
Arkato: High school students should get training on note-taking skills. Hagos: ____________. Not now; they can
have it when they join university.
o: This could save their study time
g12-english.e: Hagos disagrees with Arkato's proposal by saying 'Not now', so 'I don't agree with you' is the correct response.

g12-english.t:
Since its discovery back in 1981 G.C, HIV/AIDS is believed to have remained largely a serious problem among
those having many sexual partners.
g12-english.e: The term 'promiscuous' is defined as having many casual or transient sexual relationships or partners.

g12-english.t:
When we were in Gambella, every day after work, we _________________ sit by the river watching fishers
caught the big fish called 'gur' and made a lot of money out of it.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'used to' is used to describe past habits or states that no longer occur, fitting the context of what they did 'every day after work' when they were in Gambella. (1)

g12-english.t: be who stories learn there about are to many couldn't how rich people.
o: Stories are there about many rich people who couldn't learn how to be.
Stories about how many people are there who couldn't learn to be rich.
Many rich people are there who couldn't learn about stories.
There are many stories about people who couldn't learn how to be rich.
g12-english.e: Option A correctly arranges the words into a natural and grammatically sound English sentence: 'There are many stories about people who couldn't learn how to be rich.'

g12-english.t:
_________ Berhe ________ Umod tampered with this computer. I haven't seen them around and I think they
were out of office the whole day.
g12-english.e: The correlative conjunction 'Neither...nor' is used to join two negative options, which is confirmed by the speaker stating they haven't seen either person all day.

g12-english.t: Ali:____________________ Almaz: That sounds reasonable.
o: Did she buy a new purse?
g12-english.e: 'That sounds reasonable' is a natural response accepting or approving a proposal or suggestion, such as 'Shall we go for coffee?'.

g12-english.t: Yoyo: how long does it take to Dire Dawa? Yaya:____________________
g12-english.e: 'How long does it take?' asks about travel time, and 'It depends on your driving' directly addresses the duration.

g12-english.t:
If he is visually impaired , tell him he should learn how to use braille. Otherwise, things will be hard for him when
it comes to reading and writing.
g12-english.e: In this context, "visually impaired" refers to a person who has a visual disability, making "disabled" the most appropriate synonym.

g12-english.t:
a. They make their home in buildings, gardens, etc. b. Ants are found everywhere in the world. c. In the summer,
ants collect food for the winter season. d. They are very hardworking insects.
g12-english.e: The sequence 'b-a-c-d' is highly logical because 'b' states where ants are found generally, 'a' specifies their local homes, 'c' describes their food-gathering habit, and 'd' concludes that they are hardworking based on that habit.

g12-english.t:
Bubu: Nobody likes me because I’m poor. I’ll leave this school and find another one. Kena: What do you mean? I
carry around ________________ you do. Just keep calm.
g12-english.e: 'Money' is an uncountable noun, so the comparative form 'less money than' is grammatically correct to compare the amounts of money they carry.

g12-english.t:
They still argue that the quality of education is steadily improving. Obviously they are trying to fool us, but we
____________ the idea.
g12-english.e: To 'buy' an idea or explanation is an idiom meaning to believe or accept it; thus, 'never buy the idea' means they do not believe the claim.

g12-english.t: It has been a strongly brutal summer with very hot weather conditions.
g12-english.e: 'Brutal' when describing weather conditions means severe, unforgiving, or 'harsh'.

g12-english.t: Most of us are not modest enough to learn from others. We always think we are the best.
g12-english.e: To be 'modest' means to have a humble estimate of one's own merits, so 'humble' is the correct synonym.

g12-english.t: The most appropriate closing for a business letter is:
g12-english.e: "With regards" (or "Best regards") is a standard, polite, and formal closing for a professional business letter, unlike the other informal options.

g12-english.t:
The government should take measures on companies that ________ children under 18 by allowing their
employment with them. Such practice is globally unaccepdata.
g12-english.e: Employing children under 18 is globally considered child labor, which 'exploits' children rather than protecting them.

g12-english.t: Rawda: Would you like something to drink? Fatuma: ______________________
o: That is exactly what I see.
I would like tea if you don't mind.
Interesting to be here with you.
g12-english.e: When offered a drink, Option D ('I would like tea if you don't mind') is a polite, natural, and direct way to accept the offer.

g12-english.t: A father, a mother and children who live together make up a family.
g12-english.e: The phrasal verb 'make up' in this context means to form or constitute something.

g12-english.t: Muse: have you heard that Belete was released? Shoa: _________________
o: What good news! When was that?
Is Belete a businessman by profession?
I know. He severely criticizes the system.
g12-english.e: Hearing that someone has been released from detention typically elicits relief and a follow-up question, making 'What good news! When was that?' the most natural response.

g12-english.t:
My friends are _______ all over the country and I don't have an problem wherever I go. I have no worries of
where to stay or what to eat.
g12-english.e: 'Scattered' is the standard adjective used to describe friends or people being spread out across different locations in a country. (1)

g12-english.t:
Alemu: Sounds like you had a boring day. Did anything interesting happen?
Feyissa: _____________________
o: Many things happen in this city.
Often many things happen, but few may take our attention.
g12-english.e: To answer the yes/no question 'Did anything interesting happen?' in the context of having a boring day, 'Not really. Don't think so.' is the most natural fit.

g12-english.t: In a formal letter which of the following could be optional?
g12-english.e: A formal letter must carry the date, the address of the person you are writing to, and a salutation such as Dear Mr. Kebede. Without them the letter cannot be filed or answered. The subject heading, the short line naming the topic, is helpful but not required, so it is the optional part.

g12-english.t: I ____________ with you, Abel; irregular class attendance isn't the cause of your failure.
g12-english.e: 'Disagree' is a stative verb used in the simple present tense to state a current opinion or stance.

g12-english.t: You _______________ speak to him like that. After all, he is your elder brother and deserves some respect.
g12-english.e: The modal 'ought not to' is used to express moral obligation or strong advice, which fits the context of respecting an elder brother.

g12-english.t: Kedija: we've got loads of homework tonight, haven't we? Fayine:________________
g12-english.e: 'Yes, in three subjects' directly and grammatically answers the confirmation-seeking tag question about having a large amount of homework.

g12-english.t: Abraham: You should really apologize to your parents. Tizazu:______________________
o: Why? I don't care what they think!
g12-english.e: Option A logically responds to the recommendation to apologize by expressing defiance ('Why? I don't care what they think!'). (1)

g12-english.t:
We do not understand why he always comes so late. If he arrives on time like his friends, he _________ the
opportunity to meet us and get the necessary assistance.
g12-english.e: This is a first conditional sentence ('If + simple present, will + base verb'), so 'will have' is the correct form for the main clause.

g12-english.t: Choose the alternative with a correct spelling.
g12-english.e: 'Cooperative' is spelled correctly, while the other options contain spelling errors ('optimistic', 'communication', 'distinguished').

g12-english.t: I couldn't hear what the teacher was saying during the lesson, but I think I ______ him to be louder.
g12-english.e: 'Could have asked' is used to express a past capability or possibility that was not realized.

g12-english.t: They wasted some time at the beginning and now they are under pressure to
g12-english.e: The noun 'pressure' in the phrase 'under pressure' refers to a state of stress or mental/emotional strain, which is closest in meaning to 'tension'.

g12-english.t: Tourist: What do I need to visit the museum? Guard: ...
o: You must get permission from the manager.
You can get permission from the manager.
You have got permission from the manager.
You are sure to get permission from the manager.
g12-english.e: What do I need asks about a requirement, and must states a requirement: you must get permission from the manager. Option A, can get permission, says that permission is possible to obtain, which answers a different question, and it leaves the tourist unsure whether it is needed

g12-english.t: By the year 2020, the cure for both HIV/AIDS and Ebola_________________.
g12-english.e: The time marker 'by the year 2020' (viewed from 2007 EC / 2014-2015 GC) requires the future perfect passive form, 'will have been discovered'.

g12-english.t:
a. One of my favourite things to do is wash my car. b. People say they can tell about a person by their shoes. c.
Here is the thoughtful process I follow to wash my car. d. A clean car says I?m proud and I feel good about my
self. e. I say that you can tell about a person by how clean his car is.
g12-english.e: The paragraph builds an idea before it uses it. Sentence b reports what other people say about shoes, e gives the writer's own version about cars, d explains what a clean car says about him, a tells us washing his car is a favourite thing, and c promises the process, which is what a following paragraph would give. That is b e d a c. D is tempting because a sounds like an opening line, but starting there leaves b and e stranded with nothing to lead into.

g12-english.t:
According to the passage, the drought and famine of Wollo demonstrates the relationship between climate
change and
g12-english.e: Historically, the Wollo famine is cited as a classic example of how climatic factors interact with political neglect and a lack of governance.

g12-english.t: A room _______________for you at Hilton Hotel.
g12-english.e: The subject 'A room' receives the action, requiring the present perfect passive voice 'has been reserved'.

g12-english.t: we studied together at college, but I________________her ever since.
g12-english.e: The time expression 'ever since' refers to a period extending from a specific past point up to the present, which requires the present perfect tense ('haven't seen').

g12-english.t: In my life, I ______________ had money counted in four digits. Poor me!
g12-english.e: "Never" carries the negative on its own, and the present perfect covers experience from the past up to now: "In my life, I have never had money counted in four digits." B is the trap because it doubles the negative with "haven't" and "never" together, and standard English uses one negative word for one negative meaning.

g12-english.t:
If what you are telling me is true, then I _______ straight away and register with them. I don't want to miss the
opportunity.
g12-english.e: This is a first conditional structure expressing a spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking based on a condition ('If what you are telling me is true'), which requires the future simple 'will go'.

g12-english.t:
I say we should not question the competence of the new team. Each member is ________ those we had in the
last round. They may have another problem and that should be studied.
g12-english.e: The comparative construction of equality uses the format 'as + adjective + as', making 'as experienced as' the correct choice.

g12-english.t:
__________ the pilot and his crew recognized the plane had a problem. However, they didn't say anything lest
disturbing the passengers.
g12-english.e: The correlative conjunction 'both... and...' is used to connect two subjects ('the pilot' and 'his crew') who performed the same action.

g12-english.t: Secretary: how do yo do, sir? Vistor:______________
o: I am fine. How do you do?
I am fine. How are you?
Very well, how do you do?
g12-english.e: In formal English, the conventional and idiomatic reply to the greeting 'How do you do?' is simply 'How do you do?'.

g12-english.t: I went home because I...
g12-english.e: The main verb went is in the past, so the reason clause has to be in the past too: I felt bored. Feel becomes felt, and the ed ending is not used for it. Option B swaps in the wrong verb, since fell comes from fall, which means to drop down, not to have a feeling.

g12-english.t: Interviewer: __________________. Jorgie: Actually, my interest is in fashion designing
o: Could you tell me about your interest?
Did I hear you like fashion designing?
Why are you interested in fashion designing?
g12-english.e: The response specifies what the speaker's interest is, making 'Could you tell me about your interest?' the most logical prompt among the choices.

g12-english.t: Bulti: The enemy is approaching. We have to evacuate soon. Gebrai:___________________
o: I think, they have soldiers in excess of us.
This area is ideal for them.
Perhaps, we might need to do that.
g12-english.e: Bulti suggests that they need to evacuate, and Gebrai's reply 'Perhaps, we might need to do that' directly addresses and considers that proposed action. (1)

g12-english.t: Bekalu : How ______ do you watch television?
g12-english.e: 'How often' is the standard question phrase used to ask about the frequency of an activity like watching television.

g12-english.t:
a. You can use it to talk with your friends or family, for example. b. A mobile phone is a very useful device to get
connected with others. c. A mobile phone call can be made in so many ways. d. These days, everyone has a
mobile phone.
g12-english.e: Option A (b-d-a-c) is the most coherent sequence because 'b' introduces the mobile phone, 'd' states its widespread ownership, 'a' gives an example of its use, and 'c' expands on how calls are made. (1)

g12-english.t: Which one of the paragraphs below emphasizes the need for showing one's own competence in tests?
g12-english.e: Paragraph 4 explains that hiring someone else to do your work is wrong because 'you are not showing your own competence, you are showing someone else's.'

g12-english.t: You think __________ a child. How do you tell me that nothing will happen if you jump down from this height?
g12-english.e: The preposition 'like' is used here to mean 'in the same way as' to compare the person's thinking to that of a child. (1)

g12-english.t: Customer: Do you have a changing room? Shop assistant: _____
g12-english.e: The customer asks whether the shop has a changing room, so the answer confirms it and shows where it is: 'Certainly, it's over there', option D. Option A is the tempting misreading: a changing room is where you try clothes on, not a place where goods are exchanged.

g12-english.t:
Are those two girls from the same family? They look alike and _____ I see them together, even in odd kind of
places.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'most of the time' functions as an adverbial of frequency that logically connects with 'always see them together' and fits grammatically in the sentence. (1)

g12-english.t:
Zeru: In my free time, I go swimming in Sheraton Hotel. Molla: ___________________ Zeru: Since 2015. That's
for about 9 years now.
o: When did you start doing that?
How long ago did you start this hobby?
How long have you been doing it?
How long did you do that?
g12-english.e: The present perfect continuous question 'How long have you been doing it?' is used to ask about the duration of an ongoing habit or hobby, which perfectly matches the response 'Since 2015. That's for about 9 years now.'

g12-english.t: Mother: Tell me why schools are closed in Kiremt in Ethiopia. Daughter: ___________________________
g12-english.e: When asked why schools are closed, the daughter politely admits she does not know by saying, 'I haven't any clue, Mom.' (1)

g12-english.t: I __________my homework when you knocked at the door.
g12-english.e: The past continuous ('was doing') is used for an ongoing past action that was interrupted by another action in the past simple ('knocked').

g12-english.t:
Deboch: national exams should not continue. Teklu: probably, you may be right. Deboch: since we cannot do
away with exams, regions may need to set their own. Teklu: this may be good idea, but there is the issue of
standard. Deboch: the federal ministry may set the basic standards. Teklu: ________
o: well, I may agree with you.
g12-english.e: Deboch successfully addresses Teklu's concern about standards, leading Teklu to concede and agree with the proposed solution ('well, I may agree with you').

g12-english.t: Nardos: I heard you were the only person to get the job. Well done! Girma: ________
g12-english.e: The standard and polite response to congratulations ('Well done!') is 'Thank you.'

g12-english.t: Can anyone tell me _______ book this is? It has been lying here for months.
g12-english.e: The possessive determiner 'whose' is required to ask about the ownership of the book.

g12-english.t:
By the time you come for your next holiday, they ____________ the construction of the hotel. Surely, you will be
staying there.
g12-english.e: The future perfect tense ('will have completed') is required because of the time marker 'By the time', indicating that the construction will be finished before the next holiday.

g12-english.t: My mother usually wakes up at ______________and goes to her bedroom late at evening.
g12-english.e: 'Dawn' refers to the first appearance of light in the sky before sunrise, which fits perfectly as the time one would wake up in the morning.

g12-english.t: Akalu: What was the party like? Lulu: ______________.
o: Do you think people liked it?
About a thousand people were invited.
g12-english.e: The question 'What was the party like?' asks for an evaluation or description of the event, perfectly answered by 'I think, it was OK.'

g12-english.t: Alemu has been teaching Geography ______________ he was Bale Robe.
g12-english.e: The present perfect continuous tense is used with 'since' to indicate the starting point of an action that continues up to the present.

g12-english.t: According to the fourth paragraph, nonpoint pollutants come from which one of the following?
g12-english.e: Nonpoint source pollution comes from diffuse, land-based sources, with agricultural runoff from farming being one of the primary contributors.

g12-english.t: You: Are you married, Zahara? Zahara:________________
g12-english.e: 'Are you married?' is a yes/no question, and 'No, I'm not' provides the direct and grammatically correct short response.

g12-english.t: You have ___ to do at home this afternoon, so you can't go out.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'so you can't go out' indicates that the person is busy, meaning they have 'something' to do at home.

g12-english.t: You know this is a literate society.
g12-english.e: 'Literate' refers to the ability to read and write and is closely associated with being 'educated'.

g12-english.t:
Your wife _____________ since 9.00 am but you don't even call and apologize for not being able to arrive until
now. What excuse do you have for this?
g12-english.e: The present perfect continuous tense 'has been waiting' is used for an action that started in the past (9:00 am) and is still continuing up to the present.

g12-english.t: Let me go and check if the car is ready. It _______________________ when I came this morning.
g12-english.e: The past continuous passive form 'was being fixed' is used here to describe an action that was in progress in the past when another action occurred ('when I came this morning').

g12-english.t:
Musa: How is your father? I heard he has been hospitalized. Robale: _____ He seems to need further
investigation.
g12-english.e: The second half of Robale's line says his father seems to need further investigation, so the report on his health has to be a poor one. "Not very well" fits. A is tempting because it is a normal answer to "How is your father", but a man who is very well would not need more tests.

g12-english.t: You I you say to for did want for all us thank.
o: I did want you for all for us to say thank you.
I want to say thank you for all you did for us.
you want to say I thank you for all did for us.
you say I want to thank you for all did for us.
g12-english.e: Option A forms a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence ('I want to say thank you for all you did for us') using all the given words exactly once.

g12-english.t: The newly married couple has just gone to Hawassa for the ___.
g12-english.e: A 'honeymoon' is a holiday taken by a newly married couple, making it the correct term for this context.

g12-english.t: Conservation of natural resources is one of the key duties of any society.
g12-english.e: The 'conservation' of natural resources refers to their preservation and 'protection' from exploitation and destruction.

g12-english.t: Worldwide, a large number of organizations ______ children who have lost their parents in death.
g12-english.e: Organizations provide financial and material support to orphans, which is best described as 'sponsoring' them.

g12-english.t:
It would be embarrassing________________ the truth. The good thing was that no one told her what had
happened.
g12-english.e: 'Were she to find out' is an inverted second conditional structure functioning as 'if she were to find out', which matches the conditional modal 'would be' in the main clause. (1)

g12-english.t: Customer:______________? Shop assistant: It's 1500 birr.
g12-english.e: The shop assistant gives the price of an item ('1500 birr'), which corresponds to the question 'How much is this camera?'.

g12-english.t: Which word is wrongly spelt?
g12-english.e: The word "Jiboutian" is misspelled; the correct spelling of the demonym for someone from Djibouti is "Djiboutian" with a silent 'D'.

g12-english.t: Of the words given below, which one from paragraph 3 can be replaced by 'dislike' ?
g12-english.e: 'Abhor' means to regard with disgust and hatred, so it is the best synonym for 'dislike' in the given context.

g12-english.t: As docile is to tamed so is awesome to ________
g12-english.e: 'Docile' and 'tamed' are synonyms; similarly, 'awesome' and 'grand' share the meaning of being magnificent and inspiring awe.

g12-english.t: The old systems did not impose additional financial burden on the business community. __________
g12-english.e: To show agreement with a negative statement, we use 'Neither + auxiliary verb + subject'. Since the first sentence uses the past simple auxiliary 'did not', the correct addition is 'Neither did the new systems'.

g12-english.t: The police officers are trying to trace the prisoners that have escaped the prison.
g12-english.e: To 'trace' in this context means to track down or discover the location of the escaped prisoners, which is synonymous with 'locate'.

g12-english.t: Benti: This is the Toyota car we bought last week. Isn't it beautiful? Nani: _______________
o: What? Is that really your car?
Oh no! I know you can't afford it.
What a great car! Really exciting!
g12-english.e: Benti invites agreement and admiration with the question 'Isn't it beautiful?', to which an enthusiastic compliment like 'What a great car! Really exciting!' is the most socially appropriate response.

g12-english.t:
Their graduation will be in June. Then, they will do some shopping and tour around probably for three weeks and 
by the end of July, they definitely __________ back.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'by the end of July' is a future time marker that requires the Future Perfect tense ('will have come') to show an action completed before that point.

g12-english.t: my sister _________________ me a parcel two weeks ago, but I received it only yesterday.
g12-english.e: The definite past time marker 'two weeks ago' requires the simple past tense 'sent'.

g12-english.t:
If you have to go abroad for your education, one of the things you have to be worried about is____________. You 
have to be sure of where you are going to stay before you leave this country.
g12-english.e: 'Accommodation' refers to lodging or a place to live, which directly matches the hint 'where you are going to stay'.

g12-english.t: You: why did you leave the party early last night? Rahel:__________________
g12-english.e: The question asks for a reason ('Why...'), and 'I didn't feel well' provides a valid reason for leaving early.

g12-english.t:
Tariku: The personnel manager, without existing evidence, fired Genet from her job. ______ that we will
reconsider the General Manager's case again because we need further evidence for her dishonesty.
g12-english.e: 'I am convinced that we will reconsider...' makes logical sense in this context as they lack evidence and thus need to reevaluate the case.

g12-english.t:
The price of fertilizer has kept soaring for the last five or six years. Unless they are provided with some form of
___________, our farmers cannot afford it and will undoubtedly be in a problem.
g12-english.e: A 'subsidy' is a sum of money granted by the state or a public body to help keep the price of a commodity or service low, which fits the context of farmers struggling to afford soaring fertilizer prices.

g12-english.t: Tomorrow, Sofanit ___ her assignments the whole day.
g12-english.e: The phrase 'Tomorrow ... the whole day' indicates an action that will be in progress over a duration of time in the future, which requires the future continuous tense 'will be doing'.

g12-english.t:
Everything they are doing is so rubbish that you would consider firing them. Their former boss told me he had no 
satisfaction with any one of them.
g12-english.e: The word 'satisfaction' is synonymous with 'contentment', which refers to the state of being happy and satisfied with someone's work.

g12-english.t: Uncle: when are you going to marry? You:_______________
o: I'm going to college next year.
I don't actually live here after marriage.
g12-english.e: The question asks 'when', and 'not until I'm 45' specifies the time/age the speaker intends to marry.

g12-english.t: The purchasers should be accountable for what has happened.____________ piece is faulty.
g12-english.e: 'Every' is used with a singular countable noun ('piece') to indicate that all items in a group share a particular quality.

g12-english.t: Husband: Where would you like us to go for dinner? Wife: ___________________I like their French toast.
o: How about trying Haile Grand Hotel?
I do not care about dinner tonight.
Is your sister going with us?
I do not have enough money for dinner.
g12-english.e: The wife suggests a dining location ('How about trying Haile Grand Hotel?') and supports her suggestion by mentioning their French toast, directly answering the husband's question.

g12-english.t: Applicants should have________ experience in the relevant area to apply for the job.
g12-english.e: Job applications frequently require 'prior' experience, meaning experience gained before applying.

g12-english.t: ____________ it has drastically changed the cultures of many nations and created undisciplined citizens.
g12-english.e: 'However' is used as a transition word at the beginning of a sentence to contrast a new point with a previously stated context.

g12-english.t: I don't get along with most of my classmates.
g12-english.e: 'Get along with' means to have a harmonious relationship with someone, which is closest in meaning to 'agree' among the provided choices.

g12-english.t: Aunt: ________ Lojo: sure
o: you will give me the bread.
pass me the bread, will you?
g12-english.e: 'Pass me the bread, will you?' is a polite request that can be naturally responded to with 'Sure.'

g12-english.t: My brother had never expected to get the job. He was really ______________ when he offered it.
g12-english.e: The participial adjective ending in '-ed' ('amazed') is used to describe how a person feels, whereas '-ing' adjectives describe the thing causing the feeling.

g12-english.t: Although the doctor has warned him several times, he hasn't stopped ___ yet.
g12-english.e: The verb 'stop' followed by a gerund ('drinking') means to discontinue an activity or habit, which fits the context of ignoring a doctor's warning.

g12-english.t: If you enjoy ________, you can register with us and trek around the city every Sunday in the afternoon.
g12-english.e: The verb 'enjoy' is transitively followed by a gerund (-ing form), making 'walking' the correct choice.

g12-english.t:
We are so regretful that we didn't take necessary measures to stop the tyranny that went on in prisons of this
country. No doubt, we would be held responsible.
g12-english.e: The adjective 'regretful' is synonymous with 'remorseful', expressing sorrow or guilt for a past action or failure to act.

g12-english.t: You will start running__________ the bell rings. Otherwise, you will be disqualified from the competition.
g12-english.e: 'After' is the only conjunction that makes chronological sense here, showing that the action of running must follow the ringing of the bell to avoid disqualification.

g12-english.t: Dessalegn: _____________________ Chaltu: Yes, you are.
o: I'm working to help you, amn't i?
You are trying to help me, aren't you?
There are a number of solutions, aren't there?
g12-english.e: The standard question tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I?'. When the speaker asks 'I'm genuine, aren't I?', the listener correctly responds with 'Yes, you are.'

g12-english.t:
There is a huge increase in the number of newly set up educational institutions during the last thirty years but
we need to work on quality as well.
g12-english.e: 'Huge' and 'massive' are synonyms used to describe something of exceptionally large size or scale. (1)

g12-english.t: I haven't started my homework yet but I________ it by 4:00 in the afternoon. Submission time is 4:15 p.m.
g12-english.e: The prepositional phrase 'by 4:00 in the afternoon' specifies a deadline in the future, which requires the future perfect tense ('will have done').

g12-english.t:
____________________ in the country can you find people free of such bias. Better take it as a norm and live
with it.
g12-english.e: Negative adverbs of place like 'Nowhere' trigger subject-auxiliary inversion ('can you find') at the beginning of a sentence.

g12-english.t:
Teacher: Alemu has just made a good point on how we can improve education in our country.________ Taye?
Taye: Yes. We should have well-trained teachers.
o: What is another idea you have
Would you like to add anything
g12-english.e: The teacher is opening the floor to Taye to contribute to the discussion. 'Would you like to add anything' is a polite and common way to invite additional input.

g12-english.t:
I can see your point of argument but _________________ the officials are honest when it comes to denouncing
corruption. One of them was caught red-handed by the police a fortnight ago.
g12-english.e: The speaker contrasts the listener's point of argument with a counterexample, indicating skepticism; 'I am not convinced that' correctly introduces this doubt.

g12-english.t:
I usually get nervous at the beginning of interview sessions but as time goes, I become________ and get back
to normal.
g12-english.e: The adjective 'calm' provides the exact contrast to feeling 'nervous' at the beginning of the interview.

g12-english.t: Which one of the following has an error in capitalization?
o: Lake Tana is the source of the Blue Nile.
I do not go to work on Fridays.
The major religions in Ethiopia are Christianity and Islam.
g12-english.e: All three sentences follow the rules: each starts with a capital letter, and the proper nouns Lake Tana, Blue Nile, Fridays, Ethiopia, Christianity and Islam are capitalized. So the answer is None of the above. Option B is the one many readers pick, because days of the week look like ordinary nouns, but English always capitalizes them.

g12-english.t:
Tourist: The roads in the city are dilapidated.
Friend: ___________________________
o: There are more pressing problems, though.
Yeah, they should have at least been patched.
You know, the world economy is in a problem.
They are better in the countryside.
g12-english.e: Answering 'Yeah, they should have at least been patched' agrees with the complaint about the dilapidated roads and suggests a minimal corrective action.

g12-english.t: In got has house all money new the her she.
o: she has got all her money in the new house.
All her money she has got in the new house.
she has got her money all in the new house.
she has all here new money got in the house.
g12-english.e: The correct syntactic arrangement is 'she has got all her money in the new house', where 'all her money' functions as the direct object of 'has got' followed by the prepositional phrase of location.

g12-english.t:
Once up on a time there was an emperor who loved to spend his money on expensive things. This is most likely
an introductory part of a writing that is:
g12-english.e: "Once upon a time there was an emperor" is the standard opening of a story, and the past tense sets up events that will follow one after another. Writing that tells a story is narrative.
